<note>A task-notification fires each time this agent stops with no live background children of its own. The user can send it another message and resume it, so the same task-id may notify more than once.</note>
<result>I found how every API supplies most of the card's fields. The weakest spots are filament per slot (Moonraker, Prusa, Duet, Elegoo), the printer model (Klipper, PrusaLink, Flashforge), and readable error text (Bambu, Flashforge, Creality, Elegoo). Anything I could not confirm from a source is marked unverified.

## Bambu (MQTT on the LAN, plus FTPS)
- **Camera:** X1 and P2S serve `rtsps://IP:322/streaming/live/1` with user `bblp` and the LAN access code. On H2S and H2D the same stream is off until enabled on the touchscreen. P1 and A1 send JPEG frames over TLS on port 6000, after a binary login packet. [video.md](https://github.com/Doridian/OpenBambuAPI/blob/main/video.md) The MQTT report carries `ipcam.rtsp_url`; the value `"disable"` means LAN live view is off. [ha-bambulab models.py](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/greghesp/ha-bambulab/main/custom_components/bambu_lab/pybambu/models.py)
- **Job, progress, time left:** `subtask_name` / `gcode_file`, `mc_percent`, `mc_remaining_time`. [mqtt.md](https://github.com/Doridian/OpenBambuAPI/blob/main/mqtt.md) The docs give no unit for remaining time; minutes is commonly assumed but unverified.
- **Thumbnail:** not in MQTT. ha-bambulab downloads the job's `.3mf` from the printer and caches it for the cover image. [models.py](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/greghesp/ha-bambulab/main/custom_components/bambu_lab/pybambu/models.py) The plate PNG path inside the 3mf is unverified.
- **Model:** `info.get_version.module[]` has `name`, `hw_ver`, `sn`, `sw_ver`; there is no product-name field in those docs. [mqtt.md](https://github.com/Doridian/OpenBambuAPI/blob/main/mqtt.md) ha-bambulab uses `info.device_type`, but where that comes from is unverified.
- **Nozzle:** `nozzle_diameter`, a string such as `"0.4"`. [mqtt.md](https://github.com/Doridian/OpenBambuAPI/blob/main/mqtt.md)
- **Filament:** `ams.ams[].tray[].tray_type` and `tray_color` (RRGGBBAA), plus `vt_tray` for the external spool and `tray_now` for the active one. [mqtt.md](https://github.com/Doridian/OpenBambuAPI/blob/main/mqtt.md)
- **Errors:** `hms[]`, `print_error`, `mc_print_error_code` are codes only. ha-bambulab turns them into text with `get_HMS_error_text` and `get_print_error_text`, and treats `50348044` as a user cancel. [models.py](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/greghesp/ha-bambulab/main/custom_components/bambu_lab/pybambu/models.py) Where its lookup table comes from is unverified.
- **Last outcome:** `gcode_state` FINISH or FAILED; a cancel is told apart by that error code. The previous job's data is cleared only when the next job starts, so the name stays until then. [models.py](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/greghesp/ha-bambulab/main/custom_components/bambu_lab/pybambu/models.py)
- **Temperatures:** `nozzle_temper`, `nozzle_target_temper`, `bed_temper`, `bed_target_temper`. [mqtt.md](https://github.com/Doridian/OpenBambuAPI/blob/main/mqtt.md)

## Moonraker / Klipper
- **Camera:** `/server/webcams/list` returns `stream_url`, `snapshot_url` and `service`. A URL may be relative to the Moonraker host, and `snapshot_url` is empty when the camera has no snapshot. [webcams](https://moonraker.readthedocs.io/en/latest/external_api/webcams/)
- **Job:** `print_stats.filename`. **Progress:** `display_status.progress` (from M73, falling back to file position) or `virtual_sdcard.progress`. [Status Reference](https://www.klipper3d.org/Status_Reference.html)
- **Time left: computed.** Take `estimated_time` from the file's metadata, in seconds, and subtract `print_stats.print_duration`. [file_manager](https://moonraker.readthedocs.io/en/latest/external_api/file_manager/), [Status Reference](https://www.klipper3d.org/Status_Reference.html)
- **Thumbnail:** metadata `thumbnails[]` with `width`, `height`, `relative_path`. The path is relative to the G-code file's folder, and you fetch it through `/server/files/gcodes/...`. That fetch path is my inference; it is not documented as such. [file_manager](https://moonraker.readthedocs.io/en/latest/external_api/file_manager/)
- **Model:** none in the [Status Reference](https://www.klipper3d.org/Status_Reference.html). The printer reports nothing; the slicer's name is in metadata `slicer`.
- **Nozzle:** the live extruder object has no nozzle diameter. The file's metadata has `nozzle_diameter`. Reading the `[extruder] nozzle_diameter` config option through the `configfile` object is unverified.
- **Filament:** metadata `filament_type` and `filament_name` describe the file, not what is loaded. Happy Hare exposes `printer.mmu.material` and `printer.mmu.gate_color_rgb` ([Happy Hare](https://www.github.com/tnap1979/Happy-Hare), [LED wiki](https://github.meowingcats01.workers.dev/moggieuk/Happy-Hare/wiki/Led-Support)). A Moonraker database namespace called `lane_data` is used by an OrcaSlicer-fork script ([script](https://git.trueserve.org/PublicCodeMirror/OrcaSlicer-bambulab/raw/branch/main/scripts/test_moonraker_lane_data.py)). I could not confirm Moonraker documents it.
- **Errors:** `webhooks.state_message` and `print_stats.message`, which are readable text. [Status Reference](https://www.klipper3d.org/Status_Reference.html)
- **Last outcome:** `/server/history/list?limit=1` returns `status` (completed, cancelled, error, klippy_shutdown, in_progress), `filename` and `end_time`. This survives the end of the job. [history](https://moonraker.readthedocs.io/en/latest/external_api/history/)
- **Temperatures:** `extruder.temperature` / `target` and `heater_bed.temperature` / `target`. [Status Reference](https://www.klipper3d.org/Status_Reference.html)

## OctoPrint
- **Camera:** `/api/settings` gives `webcam.streamUrl` and `webcam.snapshotUrl`. [settings](https://docs.octoprint.org/en/master/api/settings.html) Since 1.9, webcams are provided by plugins, with the old behaviour moved into a bundled "Classic Webcam" plugin. [All3DP](https://all3dp.com/4/octoprint-receives-1-9-0-update-with-host-of-qol-changes/) The snapshot URL is often `localhost`, as seen from the server, so a remote client may not reach it. [forum](https://community.octoprint.org/t/unable-to-change-the-webcam-address/52031) I found no documented `/api/webcams` endpoint.
- **Job, progress, time left:** `/api/job` gives `job.file.name`, `progress.completion` and `progress.printTimeLeft` (units unstated). [job](https://docs.octoprint.org/en/master/api/job.html)
- **Thumbnail:** core has none. The PrusaSlicer Thumbnails plugin adds a `thumbnail` field to the file metadata. [OctoDash issue](https://github.com/UnchartedBull/OctoDash/issues/566)
- **Model and nozzle:** these come from the user-set printer profile (`name`, `model`, `extruder.nozzleDiameter`; pick the one with `current: true`), not from the printer. [printerprofiles](https://docs.octoprint.org/en/master/api/printerprofiles.html)
- **Filament:** not available.
- **Errors:** `/api/job` `error`, `/api/printer` `state.text`, and the flag `state.flags.error`. [job](https://docs.octoprint.org/en/master/api/job.html), [printer](https://docs.octoprint.org/en/master/api/printer.html)
- **Last outcome:** per file, `print.last.success` and `print.last.date`. This says success or failure only, with no cancel distinction, and you have to know which file to ask about. [files](https://docs.octoprint.org/en/master/api/files.html)
- **Temperatures:** `temperature.tool0` and `temperature.bed`, each with `actual` and `target`. [printer](https://docs.octoprint.org/en/master/api/printer.html)

## PrusaLink
All fields below come from the [PrusaLink OpenAPI spec](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/prusa3d/Prusa-Link-Web/master/spec/openapi.yaml).
- **Camera:** `/api/v1/cameras` lists `camera_id`, `config.name` and flags such as `connected`. A snapshot endpoint is unverified, and I did not confirm that MK4/XL/MINI firmware serves this endpoint.
- **Job:** `/api/v1/job` `file.display_name`, with `progress` and `time_remaining` in seconds. `/api/v1/status` also has `job.progress` and `job.time_remaining`.
- **Thumbnail:** `file.refs.thumbnail` and `file.refs.icon`.
- **Model:** no model field. `file.meta.printer_model` is what the file was sliced for.
- **Nozzle:** `/api/v1/info` `nozzle_diameter`.
- **Filament:** `/api/v1/info` has an `mmu` boolean only; per-slot data is not in the spec. `file.meta.filament_type` describes the file.
- **Errors:** `printer.status_printer.message`. The ATTENTION state carries no text.
- **Last outcome:** the states FINISHED, STOPPED and ERROR, with `job.id`. There is no history endpoint.
- **Temperatures:** `temp_nozzle`, `target_nozzle`, `temp_bed`, `target_bed`.

## Prusa Connect
This is a cloud service, not a LAN API. Its only documented public API is the camera one, where a camera pushes JPEGs with `PUT /v1/snapshot` and sends `PUT /v1/camera-info`. [camera-service docs](https://camera-service.prusa3d.com/docs/), [help](https://help.prusa3d.com/article/prusa-connect-camera-api_569012) I found no documented public API for reading printer status or snapshots, so every card field is unverified.

## Duet (RepRapFirmware object model)
All fields below come from the [object model docs](https://github.com/Duet3D/RepRapFirmware/wiki/Object-Model-Documentation) unless noted.
- **Camera:** not in the object model. The URL is set in the Duet Web Control settings and kept in the browser's local storage. [reprap wiki](https://reprap.org/wiki/Duet_Web_Control)
- **Job:** `job.file.fileName`. **Time left:** `job.timesLeft.file`, `.filament` and `.slicer`, in seconds.
- **Progress: computed.** The card has to derive it, for example from the time fields. I did not confirm a field for it.
- **Thumbnail:** `job.file.thumbnails[]`, only when the board runs with an attached computer (SBC mode).
- **Model:** `boards[].name` gives the board name, not the printer.
- **Nozzle:** none found.
- **Filament:** `move.extruders[].filament` gives a filament name only, with no colour.
- **Errors:** `state.messageBox.title` and `.message`, plus `state.displayMessage`.
- **Last outcome:** `job.lastFileName`, `lastFileCancelled`, `lastFileAborted`, `lastDuration`. These persist after the job.
- **Temperatures:** `heat.heaters[].current` and `active` / `standby`.

## Flashforge (HTTP on port 8898, `/detail`)
All fields below come from [community API docs](https://github.com/Parallel-7/flashforge-api-docs/wiki/HTTP-REST-API).
- **Camera:** `cameraStreamUrl`, an MJPEG URL that is empty when no camera is present.
- **Job:** `printFileName`. **Progress:** `printProgress`, from 0 to 1. **Time left:** `estimatedTime`, in seconds; it freezes while paused.
- **Thumbnail:** `printFileThumbUrl`, or POST `/gcodeThumb`.
- **Model:** no model field; map `pid` (35 = 5M, 36 = 5M Pro, 38 = AD5X).
- **Nozzle:** `nozzleModel`, for example `"0.4mm"`.
- **Filament (AD5X):** `matlStationInfo.slotInfos[]` with `materialName` and `materialColor`. [AD5X wiki](https://1clonegithubbyxjn.1934672944.workers.dev/Parallel-7/flashforge-api-docs/wiki/AD5X)
- **Errors:** `errorCode` is a code only.
- **Last outcome:** whether it persists is undocumented.
- **Temperatures:** `rightTemp` / `rightTargetTemp` and `platTemp` / `platTargetTemp`.

## Elegoo SDCP (Centauri Carbon)
- **Camera:** the SDCP command 386 enables the stream and returns `VideoUrl`; `CameraStatus` is an attribute. [SDCP V3 spec](https://github.com/cbd-tech/SDCP-Smart-Device-Control-Protocol-V3.0.0/blob/main/SDCP(Smart%20Device%20Control%20Protocol)_V3.0.0_EN.md) A third-party tool says the MJPEG stream is on port 3031 and allows one viewer at a time. [glama](https://glama.ai/mcp/servers/anvf7dgan5) The `/video` path is unverified.
- **Job and progress:** `PrintInfo.Filename` and `PrintInfo.Progress`.
- **Time left: computed** as `TotalTicks` minus `CurrentTicks`. [ha-elegoo status.py](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/danielcherubini/elegoo-homeassistant/main/custom_components/elegoo_printer/sdcp/models/status.py)
- **Thumbnail:** history command 321 returns `Thumbnail` per task. [SDCP spec](https://github.com/cbd-tech/SDCP-Smart-Device-Control-Protocol-V3.0.0/blob/main/SDCP(Smart%20Device%20Control%20Protocol)_V3.0.0_EN.md)
- **Model:** `MachineName` and `BrandName`. **Nozzle:** none found.
- **Filament:** a Home Assistant integration shows per-slot colour, but only by capturing the G-code through a proxy, not from the printer. [repo](https://github.com/danielcherubini/elegoo-homeassistant)
- **Errors:** `PrintInfo.ErrorNumber` is a code. History gives `ErrorStatusReason`, also a code.
- **Last outcome:** commands 320 and 321 return `TaskStatus` (completed, exceptional, stopped) with `TaskName`.
- **Temperatures:** `TempOfNozzle`, `TempTargetNozzle`, `TempOfHotbed`, `TempTargetHotbed`. [status.py](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/danielcherubini/elegoo-homeassistant/main/custom_components/elegoo_printer/sdcp/models/status.py)

## Creality K-series (websocket on port 9999)
Fields below come from [ha_creality_ws sensor.py](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/3dg1luk43/ha_creality_ws/main/custom_components/ha_creality_ws/sensor.py) unless noted.
- **Camera:** K1 serves MJPEG at `http://IP:8080/?action=stream`. K2 uses WebRTC at `IP:8000/call/webrtc_local`, and the `webrtcSupport` flag tells you which. [search summary](https://relatedrepos.com/gh/3dg1luk43/ha_creality_ws), [repo](https://github.com/3dg1luk43/ha_creality_ws)
- **Job, progress, time left:** `printFileName`, `printProgress`, and `printLeftTime` in seconds ([HA forum](https://community.home-assistant.io/t/deprecated-adding-creality-k1-max-to-ha-using-nodered-no-root-required/794457)).
- **Thumbnail:** `/downloads/original/current_print_image.png` over HTTP. [repo](https://github.com/3dg1luk43/ha_creality_ws)
- **Model:** `model`, `modelVersion`, `hostname`. **Nozzle:** none found.
- **Filament (CFS):** `boxsInfo.materialBoxs[].materials[]` with `type`, `color`, `name` and `vendor`.
- **Errors:** `err.errcode`, a code only.
- **Last outcome:** the printer does not announce a stop. The integration infers it from state changes and takes the file name from the last frame where the job was running. [repo](https://github.com/3dg1luk43/ha_creality_ws)
- **Temperatures:** `nozzleTemp` / `targetNozzleTemp` and `bedTemp0` / `targetBedTemp0`.

## Matrix
Y = the printer reports it, C = the card must compute or look it up, N = not available, ? = not confirmed.

| API | Camera | Job | % | Time left | Thumb | Model | Nozzle | Filament | Error text | Last outcome | Temps |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Bambu | Y `ipcam.rtsp_url` / port 6000 | Y `subtask_name` | Y `mc_percent` | Y `mc_remaining_time` (unit?) | C 3mf via FTPS | ? | Y `nozzle_diameter` | Y `ams…tray_type/tray_color` | C HMS lookup | Y `gcode_state` + name | Y `*_temper` |
| Moonraker | Y `/server/webcams/list` | Y `print_stats.filename` | Y `display_status.progress` | C metadata − duration | Y metadata `thumbnails` | N | ? (file metadata only) | ? Happy Hare `mmu` / `lane_data` | Y `state_message`, `message` | Y `/server/history/list` | Y `extruder`, `heater_bed` |
| OctoPrint | Y `webcam.streamUrl` | Y `job.file.name` | Y `completion` | Y `printTimeLeft` | ? plugin | user profile `model` | user profile | N | Y `error`, `state.text` | partial: `print.last.success` per file | Y `tool0`, `bed` |
| PrusaLink | ? `/api/v1/cameras` | Y `display_name` | Y `progress` | Y `time_remaining` | Y `refs.thumbnail` | N | Y `/api/v1/info` | N | Y `status_printer.message` | state only | Y `temp_*`, `target_*` |
| Prusa Connect | cloud push only | ? | ? | ? | ? | ? | ? | ? | ? | ? | ? |
| Duet | N (browser setting) | Y `job.file.fileName` | C | Y `timesLeft.*` | Y (SBC mode) `thumbnails` | board name only | ? | name only `extruders[].filament` | Y `messageBox` | Y `lastFile*` | Y `heaters[]` |
| Flashforge | Y `cameraStreamUrl` | Y `printFileName` | Y `printProgress` | Y `estimatedTime` | Y `printFileThumbUrl` | C from `pid` | Y `nozzleModel` | Y (AD5X) `slotInfos` | C `errorCode` | ? | Y `rightTemp`, `platTemp` |
| Elegoo SDCP | Y cmd 386 `VideoUrl` / port 3031 | Y `Filename` | Y `Progress` | C from ticks | Y via history | Y `MachineName` | ? | ? | C `ErrorNumber` | Y cmd 321 `TaskStatus` | Y `TempOf*` |
| Creality K | Y :8080 MJPEG / :8000 WebRTC | Y `printFileName` | Y `printProgress` | Y `printLeftTime` | Y `current_print_image.png` | Y `model` | ? | Y `boxsInfo` | C `err.errcode` | C inferred | Y `nozzleTemp`, `bedTemp0` |

Still open:

Anything I could not confirm from a source is marked unverified.

## Bambu (MQTT on the LAN, plus FTPS)
- **Camera:** X1 and P2S serve `rtsps://IP:322/streaming/live/1` with user `bblp` and the LAN access code. On H2S and H2D the same stream is off until enabled on the touchscreen. P1 and A1 send JPEG frames over TLS on port 6000, after a binary login packet. [video.md](https://github.com/Doridian/OpenBambuAPI/blob/main/video.md) The MQTT report carries `ipcam.rtsp_url`; the value `"disable"` means LAN live view is off. [ha-bambulab models.py](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/greghesp/ha-bambulab/main/custom_components/bambu_lab/pybambu/models.py)
- **Job, progress, time left:** `subtask_name` / `gcode_file`, `mc_percent`, `mc_remaining_time`. [mqtt.md](https://github.com/Doridian/OpenBambuAPI/blob/main/mqtt.md) The docs give no unit for remaining time; minutes is commonly assumed but unverified.
- **Thumbnail:** not in MQTT. ha-bambulab downloads the job's `.3mf` from the printer and caches it for the cover image. [models.py](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/greghesp/ha-bambulab/main/custom_components/bambu_lab/pybambu/models.py) The plate PNG path inside the 3mf is unverified.
- **Model:** `info.get_version.module[]` has `name`, `hw_ver`, `sn`, `sw_ver`; there is no product-name field in those docs. [mqtt.md](https://github.com/Doridian/OpenBambuAPI/blob/main/mqtt.md) ha-bambulab uses `info.device_type`, but where that comes from is unverified.
- **Nozzle:** `nozzle_diameter`, a string such as `"0.4"`. [mqtt.md](https://github.com/Doridian/OpenBambuAPI/blob/main/mqtt.md)
- **Filament:** `ams.ams[].tray[].tray_type` and `tray_color` (RRGGBBAA), plus `vt_tray` for the external spool and `tray_now` for the active one. [mqtt.md](https://github.com/Doridian/OpenBambuAPI/blob/main/mqtt.md)
- **Errors:** `hms[]`, `print_error`, `mc_print_error_code` are codes only. ha-bambulab turns them into text with `get_HMS_error_text` and `get_print_error_text`, and treats `50348044` as a user cancel. [models.py](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/greghesp/ha-bambulab/main/custom_components/bambu_lab/pybambu/models.py) Where its lookup table comes from is unverified.
- **Last outcome:** `gcode_state` FINISH or FAILED; a cancel is told apart by that error code. The previous job's data is cleared only when the next job starts, so the name stays until then. [models.py](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/greghesp/ha-bambulab/main/custom_components/bambu_lab/pybambu/models.py)
- **Temperatures:** `nozzle_temper`, `nozzle_target_temper`, `bed_temper`, `bed_target_temper`. [mqtt.md](https://github.com/Doridian/OpenBambuAPI/blob/main/mqtt.md)

## Moonraker / Klipper
- **Camera:** `/server/webcams/list` returns `stream_url`, `snapshot_url` and `service`. A URL may be relative to the Moonraker host, and `snapshot_url` is empty when the camera has no snapshot. [webcams](https://moonraker.readthedocs.io/en/latest/external_api/webcams/)
- **Job:** `print_stats.filename`. **Progress:** `display_status.progress` (from M73, falling back to file position) or `virtual_sdcard.progress`. [Status Reference](https://www.klipper3d.org/Status_Reference.html)
- **Time left: computed.** Take `estimated_time` from the file's metadata, in seconds, and subtract `print_stats.print_duration`. [file_manager](https://moonraker.readthedocs.io/en/latest/external_api/file_manager/), [Status Reference](https://www.klipper3d.org/Status_Reference.html)
- **Thumbnail:** metadata `thumbnails[]` with `width`, `height`, `relative_path`. The path is relative to the G-code file's folder, and you fetch it through `/server/files/gcodes/...`. That fetch path is my inference; it is not documented as such. [file_manager](https://moonraker.readthedocs.io/en/latest/external_api/file_manager/)
- **Model:** none in the [Status Reference](https://www.klipper3d.org/Status_Reference.html). The printer reports nothing; the slicer's name is in metadata `slicer`.
- **Nozzle:** the live extruder object has no nozzle diameter. The file's metadata has `nozzle_diameter`. Reading the `[extruder] nozzle_diameter` config option through the `configfile` object is unverified.
- **Filament:** metadata `filament_type` and `filament_name` describe the file, not what is loaded. Happy Hare exposes `printer.mmu.material` and `printer.mmu.gate_color_rgb` ([Happy Hare](https://www.github.com/tnap1979/Happy-Hare), [LED wiki](https://github.meowingcats01.workers.dev/moggieuk/Happy-Hare/wiki/Led-Support)). A Moonraker database namespace called `lane_data` is used by an OrcaSlicer-fork script ([script](https://git.trueserve.org/PublicCodeMirror/OrcaSlicer-bambulab/raw/branch/main/scripts/test_moonraker_lane_data.py)). I could not confirm Moonraker documents it.
- **Errors:** `webhooks.state_message` and `print_stats.message`, which are readable text. [Status Reference](https://www.klipper3d.org/Status_Reference.html)
- **Last outcome:** `/server/history/list?limit=1` returns `status` (completed, cancelled, error, klippy_shutdown, in_progress), `filename` and `end_time`. This survives the end of the job. [history](https://moonraker.readthedocs.io/en/latest/external_api/history/)
- **Temperatures:** `extruder.temperature` / `target` and `heater_bed.temperature` / `target`. [Status Reference](https://www.klipper3d.org/Status_Reference.html)

## OctoPrint
- **Camera:** `/api/settings` gives `webcam.streamUrl` and `webcam.snapshotUrl`. [settings](https://docs.octoprint.org/en/master/api/settings.html) Since 1.9, webcams are provided by plugins, with the old behaviour moved into a bundled "Classic Webcam" plugin. [All3DP](https://all3dp.com/4/octoprint-receives-1-9-0-update-with-host-of-qol-changes/) The snapshot URL is often `localhost`, as seen from the server, so a remote client may not reach it. [forum](https://community.octoprint.org/t/unable-to-change-the-webcam-address/52031) I found no documented `/api/webcams` endpoint.
- **Job, progress, time left:** `/api/job` gives `job.file.name`, `progress.completion` and `progress.printTimeLeft` (units unstated). [job](https://docs.octoprint.org/en/master/api/job.html)
- **Thumbnail:** core has none. The PrusaSlicer Thumbnails plugin adds a `thumbnail` field to the file metadata. [OctoDash issue](https://github.com/UnchartedBull/OctoDash/issues/566)
- **Model and nozzle:** these come from the user-set printer profile (`name`, `model`, `extruder.nozzleDiameter`; pick the one with `current: true`), not from the printer. [printerprofiles](https://docs.octoprint.org/en/master/api/printerprofiles.html)
- **Filament:** not available.
- **Errors:** `/api/job` `error`, `/api/printer` `state.text`, and the flag `state.flags.error`. [job](https://docs.octoprint.org/en/master/api/job.html), [printer](https://docs.octoprint.org/en/master/api/printer.html)
- **Last outcome:** per file, `print.last.success` and `print.last.date`. This says success or failure only, with no cancel distinction, and you have to know which file to ask about. [files](https://docs.octoprint.org/en/master/api/files.html)
- **Temperatures:** `temperature.tool0` and `temperature.bed`, each with `actual` and `target`. [printer](https://docs.octoprint.org/en/master/api/printer.html)

## PrusaLink
All fields below come from the [PrusaLink OpenAPI spec](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/prusa3d/Prusa-Link-Web/master/spec/openapi.yaml).
- **Camera:** `/api/v1/cameras` lists `camera_id`, `config.name` and flags such as `connected`. A snapshot endpoint is unverified, and I did not confirm that MK4/XL/MINI firmware serves this endpoint.
- **Job:** `/api/v1/job` `file.display_name`, with `progress` and `time_remaining` in seconds. `/api/v1/status` also has `job.progress` and `job.time_remaining`.
- **Thumbnail:** `file.refs.thumbnail` and `file.refs.icon`.
- **Model:** no model field. `file.meta.printer_model` is what the file was sliced for.
- **Nozzle:** `/api/v1/info` `nozzle_diameter`.
- **Filament:** `/api/v1/info` has an `mmu` boolean only; per-slot data is not in the spec. `file.meta.filament_type` describes the file.
- **Errors:** `printer.status_printer.message`. The ATTENTION state carries no text.
- **Last outcome:** the states FINISHED, STOPPED and ERROR, with `job.id`. There is no history endpoint.
- **Temperatures:** `temp_nozzle`, `target_nozzle`, `temp_bed`, `target_bed`.

## Prusa Connect
This is a cloud service, not a LAN API. Its only documented public API is the camera one, where a camera pushes JPEGs with `PUT /v1/snapshot` and sends `PUT /v1/camera-info`. [camera-service docs](https://camera-service.prusa3d.com/docs/), [help](https://help.prusa3d.com/article/prusa-connect-camera-api_569012) I found no documented public API for reading printer status or snapshots, so every card field is unverified.

## Duet (RepRapFirmware object model)
All fields below come from the [object model docs](https://github.com/Duet3D/RepRapFirmware/wiki/Object-Model-Documentation) unless noted.
- **Camera:** not in the object model. The URL is set in the Duet Web Control settings and kept in the browser's local storage. [reprap wiki](https://reprap.org/wiki/Duet_Web_Control)
- **Job:** `job.file.fileName`. **Time left:** `job.timesLeft.file`, `.filament` and `.slicer`, in seconds.
- **Progress: computed.** The card has to derive it, for example from the time fields. I did not confirm a field for it.
- **Thumbnail:** `job.file.thumbnails[]`, only when the board runs with an attached computer (SBC mode).
- **Model:** `boards[].name` gives the board name, not the printer.
- **Nozzle:** none found.
- **Filament:** `move.extruders[].filament` gives a filament name only, with no colour.
- **Errors:** `state.messageBox.title` and `.message`, plus `state.displayMessage`.
- **Last outcome:** `job.lastFileName`, `lastFileCancelled`, `lastFileAborted`, `lastDuration`. These persist after the job.
- **Temperatures:** `heat.heaters[].current` and `active` / `standby`.

## Flashforge (HTTP on port 8898, `/detail`)
All fields below come from [community API docs](https://github.com/Parallel-7/flashforge-api-docs/wiki/HTTP-REST-API).
- **Camera:** `cameraStreamUrl`, an MJPEG URL that is empty when no camera is present.
- **Job:** `printFileName`. **Progress:** `printProgress`, from 0 to 1. **Time left:** `estimatedTime`, in seconds; it freezes while paused.
- **Thumbnail:** `printFileThumbUrl`, or POST `/gcodeThumb`.
- **Model:** no model field; map `pid` (35 = 5M, 36 = 5M Pro, 38 = AD5X).
- **Nozzle:** `nozzleModel`, for example `"0.4mm"`.
- **Filament (AD5X):** `matlStationInfo.slotInfos[]` with `materialName` and `materialColor`. [AD5X wiki](https://1clonegithubbyxjn.1934672944.workers.dev/Parallel-7/flashforge-api-docs/wiki/AD5X)
- **Errors:** `errorCode` is a code only.
- **Last outcome:** whether it persists is undocumented.
- **Temperatures:** `rightTemp` / `rightTargetTemp` and `platTemp` / `platTargetTemp`.

## Elegoo SDCP (Centauri Carbon)
- **Camera:** the SDCP command 386 enables the stream and returns `VideoUrl`; `CameraStatus` is an attribute. [SDCP V3 spec](https://github.com/cbd-tech/SDCP-Smart-Device-Control-Protocol-V3.0.0/blob/main/SDCP(Smart%20Device%20Control%20Protocol)_V3.0.0_EN.md) A third-party tool says the MJPEG stream is on port 3031 and allows one viewer at a time. [glama](https://glama.ai/mcp/servers/anvf7dgan5) The `/video` path is unverified.
- **Job and progress:** `PrintInfo.Filename` and `PrintInfo.Progress`.
- **Time left: computed** as `TotalTicks` minus `CurrentTicks`. [ha-elegoo status.py](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/danielcherubini/elegoo-homeassistant/main/custom_components/elegoo_printer/sdcp/models/status.py)
- **Thumbnail:** history command 321 returns `Thumbnail` per task. [SDCP spec](https://github.com/cbd-tech/SDCP-Smart-Device-Control-Protocol-V3.0.0/blob/main/SDCP(Smart%20Device%20Control%20Protocol)_V3.0.0_EN.md)
- **Model:** `MachineName` and `BrandName`. **Nozzle:** none found.
- **Filament:** a Home Assistant integration shows per-slot colour, but only by capturing the G-code through a proxy, not from the printer. [repo](https://github.com/danielcherubini/elegoo-homeassistant)
- **Errors:** `PrintInfo.ErrorNumber` is a code. History gives `ErrorStatusReason`, also a code.
- **Last outcome:** commands 320 and 321 return `TaskStatus` (completed, exceptional, stopped) with `TaskName`.
- **Temperatures:** `TempOfNozzle`, `TempTargetNozzle`, `TempOfHotbed`, `TempTargetHotbed`. [status.py](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/danielcherubini/elegoo-homeassistant/main/custom_components/elegoo_printer/sdcp/models/status.py)

Fields below come from [ha_creality_ws sensor.py](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/3dg1luk43/ha_creality_ws/main/custom_components/ha_creality_ws/sensor.py) unless noted.
- **Camera:** K1 serves MJPEG at `http://IP:8080/?action=stream`. K2 uses WebRTC at `IP:8000/call/webrtc_local`, and the `webrtcSupport` flag tells you which. [search summary](https://relatedrepos.com/gh/3dg1luk43/ha_creality_ws), [repo](https://github.com/3dg1luk43/ha_creality_ws)
- **Job, progress, time left:** `printFileName`, `printProgress`, and `printLeftTime` in seconds ([HA forum](https://community.home-assistant.io/t/deprecated-adding-creality-k1-max-to-ha-using-nodered-no-root-required/794457)).
- **Thumbnail:** `/downloads/original/current_print_image.png` over HTTP. [repo](https://github.com/3dg1luk43/ha_creality_ws)
- **Model:** `model`, `modelVersion`, `hostname`. **Nozzle:** none found.
- **Filament (CFS):** `boxsInfo.materialBoxs[].materials[]` with `type`, `color`, `name` and `vendor`.
- **Errors:** `err.errcode`, a code only.
- **Last outcome:** the printer does not announce a stop. The integration infers it from state changes and takes the file name from the last frame where the job was running. [repo](https://github.com/3dg1luk43/ha_creality_ws)
- **Temperatures:** `nozzleTemp` / `targetNozzleTemp` and `bedTemp0` / `targetBedTemp0`.

# Global Claude Code Rules

## How to Communicate

Talk like a colleague explaining something out loud, not like a report.

1. **Full sentences, one idea each.** Lead with a concrete case (someone opens a file, chats twenty times, then runs out of credits) before any general point. Never pack a mechanism into a noun phrase like "hidden fair-use ceiling". Say what the person sees happen, step by step.

2. **No labels of your own.** Names you made up while working ("phase 2", "board 6a", "the M4 batch", "the three decisions") mean nothing to me. Name a thing by what it is or does. To ask about a screen, say where it is and send the picture.

3. **Ask decisions in full, as questions.** Start with "Decision needed". Give one paragraph per decision: what it is, why it's mine, the options with what each costs, and your pick. End it with a "?". Never refer to a decision by a label, a count, or the report it's in. Don't hand me a choice you could settle yourself by searching or measuring.

4. **Mark proposals as proposals.** Keep apart what the code does today, what you propose, and what I have agreed to. Never write an idea I haven't approved as if it were settled. Before calling something "my rule", find my actual words.

5. **Report outcomes, not the journey.** Leave out problems you hit and solved unless they change what I do next. For an investigation, say what the problem was, how you solved it, what you tested and the result, and what's still open. Keep it under about 500 words.

## Git Commit Policy

When the user asks to commit changes:

1. Run `git status` and `git diff` to review the changes.
2. If you are confident that both the changes are correct and the proposed commit message accurately describes them, proceed with git commit without asking for confirmation.
3. If you have any uncertainty about either, stop and ask the user for explicit confirmation before committing.

When the user asks to revert or amend commits:
1. Explain what will be reverted/amended
2. Ask for confirmation before executing any `git revert`, `git reset`, or `git commit --amend` commands
3. Only proceed after explicit user approval
4. Never revert commits without explicit user confirmation.

This applies to all git operations that modify commit history.

## Submodule Policy

**Never commit or attempt to commit submodule updates.**

When `git status` shows modified submodules (e.g., `modified: some-submodule (new commits)`):
- Do not stage or commit the submodule change
- Do not include submodules when running `git add`
- Leave submodule management to the user

## Testing Principles

1. Always test your code change unless the change is not testable.

2. If the change is not testable, highlight the reason why it's not testable to get the user's attention.

3. By default, do end-to-end testing on everything that may potentially be impacted by your change on the local dev environment.

4. Search for how the dev environment should be started if it's not obvious.

5. Look for README files in the project for related info.

6. Check if the local dev is already running before you try to start it again.

## Software Engineering Principles

1. **Don't reinvent the wheel (avoid Not Invented Here).** Before building anything, check whether the codebase or the libraries it already uses do it, and reuse that. Re-implementing something is a decision that needs a stated justification.

## Bug Fix Policy

**Never apply a fix for a bug you cannot reproduce.**

Before writing any fix:
1. Reproduce the bug first in the local dev environment.
2. If the bug cannot be reproduced locally (e.g., only manifests in release mode, requires specific device conditions, or the debug framework masks the crash), stop and tell the user — do not apply the fix.
3. A fix is only valid if you can demonstrate the broken behavior before the fix and the correct behavior after.

## Epistemic Discipline — Root Cause of Repeated Errors

**The core failure mode: confusing "generating a plausible explanation" with "knowing the answer."**

Coherent ≠ true. A narrative that feels right because it's internally consistent is not a verified fact.

Rules to follow every time:

1. **Search before asserting, not after being challenged.** The internet is always available. Use it proactively, not reactively as damage control.

2. **Explicitly label inference vs. verified fact.** If it hasn't been confirmed by a source, say "my hypothesis is..." or "I'd expect..." — never state it as fact.

3. **"I don't know yet" is a complete and correct answer.** Saying it is more helpful than fabricating a confident-sounding explanation.

## Problem Definition Before Search

**A well-defined problem statement is more valuable than a clever hypothesis.**

The discipline:
1. **Define the problem precisely first.** Strip out assumptions one by one until the statement contains only what is actually known. Remove irrelevant context (e.g. subscription type if it doesn't affect the symptom).
2. **Search for the problem directly** — not for your hypothesis. People who already solved the same problem will surface the real root cause.
3. **Let the search results form the conclusion.** Don't search to confirm what you already believe.
4. **Be flexible about scope.** Start with the most likely affected area (e.g. Discord) but stay open to other channels or systems being equally or more affected.

Searching to validate a hypothesis finds confirmation of whatever you already believed. Searching for the problem finds answers.


## GCP / kubectl Credential Policy

Always use the service account `ai-agent@tsdtechnology.iam.gserviceaccount.com` for all `gcloud` and `kubectl` operations. Before running any such command, switch to it:

```bash
gcloud config set account ai-agent@tsdtechnology.iam.gserviceaccount.com
```

The personal account `k@obico.io` is reserved for the user's own interactive CLI use and its OAuth tokens expire — do not rely on it.

## Sentry Access

- Instance: `sentry.obico.io`
- API base: `https://sentry.obico.io/api/0/`
- Auth token: `REDACTED`
- Usage: `curl -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" <api_url>`

# CLAUDE.md

JusPrin — a long-lived fork of OrcaSlicer (open-source C++17 3D slicer, wxWidgets GUI, CMake build system).

## Upstream vs. fork attribution

This checkout holds two codebases: upstream OrcaSlicer (the `upstream` remote, SoftFever/OrcaSlicer) and the JusPrin fork's changes on top of it. Fork changes include everything under `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/` and the seams the fork added inside OrcaSlicer-owned files.

- Say "OrcaSlicer does X" only for behavior upstream ships. Behavior added by a fork commit is "JusPrin does X", even when it lives in an OrcaSlicer-owned file.
- Check before attributing; the file path is not enough. Run `git blame` on the line, then `git branch -r --contains <sha> 'upstream/*'`. No upstream branch containing the commit means the fork owns it. Run `git fetch upstream` first if the remote may be stale.
- If you have not checked, say it is unverified whether the behavior is upstream or fork.

## Error handling discipline

- Do not catch an error merely because it can be caught. Catch only when the code can recover, translate the error at an abstraction boundary, or add context that is essential for diagnosis. Logging alone is not recovery.
- Represent expected states with normal control flow, not exceptions.
- Never turn an invariant violation or an "impossible" state into success or a silent no-op. Fix the invalid transition at the layer that owns the decision and let unexpected failures propagate to Sentry.
- Avoid duplicating defensive checks across layers. Keep lower-level operations strict, with their preconditions enforced by the caller that owns the workflow.
- If concurrency makes an invalid state reachable, fix the ordering or synchronization instead of suppressing the resulting error.
- Suppress an error only when it is genuinely expected and safely recoverable; document the reason and cover it with a test. Never broadly swallow unexpected errors.
- Prefer removing the root cause over reducing the visibility of its symptoms. Tests should encode valid transitions and assert that invalid ones remain visible.

## Build Commands

```bash
# macOS
cmake --build build/arm64 --config RelWithDebInfo --target all --

# Linux
cmake --build build --config RelWithDebInfo --target all --

# Windows (replace %build_type% with Debug/Release/RelWithDebInfo)
cmake --build . --config %build_type% --target ALL_BUILD -- -m
```

Node/npm is required to build the Agent and Home pages, or configure with `-DJUSPRIN_BUILD_WEB=OFF` and supply the bundles.

### Building on a shared machine

Several agent sessions build on the same Mac at once. Without a limit, ninja runs one compile job per core plus two, so every build you start can take the whole machine. In 2026-10 one session stacked four builds in one build directory: 56 clang processes on 12 cores. It kept restarting its build to change targets and never limited the job count.

- Before starting a build, check `uptime` and `pgrep -fl ninja`. If the load is already above the core count, wait or build less.
- Limit jobs: `cmake --build … -- -j4`.
- Decide the full target list before starting. Never restart a running build to add or change targets: let it finish, then build the rest.
- Run one build per build directory. Two ninja processes in one directory compete and can leave its records inconsistent.
- Stopping a build means stopping ninja. `pkill -f "cmake --build …"` kills only the cmake wrapper, and ninja keeps compiling. Start long builds in their own process group (`perl -e 'setpgrp(0,0); exec @ARGV' cmake --build …`) and stop them with `kill -- -<pgid>`. Then confirm with `pgrep -fl ninja` before building again.
- When a build is slow, count your own compile processes before blaming the load on other sessions.
- Reuse an existing build where the task allows. Ask before configuring a fresh full-app build the task does not require.

## Testing

Catch2 framework. Tests in `tests/` directory.

```bash
cd build && ctest --output-on-failure           # all tests
ctest --test-dir ./tests/libslic3r              # individual suite
ctest --test-dir ./tests/fff_print
```

Printer UI without hardware: `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Testing/README.md` (Bambu in-process fake). Isolated `--datadir`; do not drive another JusPrin instance.

## Code Style

- C++17, selective C++20. PascalCase classes, snake_case functions/variables
- `#pragma once` for headers. Smart pointers and RAII preferred
- Parallelization via TBB — be mindful of shared state
- Wording: a file or object is "opened", "imported", "loaded" or "added", never "arrived". "Arrive" is fine for messages, responses, events and lists. `AgentUI/src/wording.test.ts` guards the text the model reads.
- Wording the model reads calls the product "the app", never Orca or OrcaSlicer: the model speaks as the app, and a second name reads as a second program. `AgentUI/src/wording.test.ts` guards this too. Log lines may name Orca. A throw may only if it never reaches the model: tool results forward save and open errors as they are, and the guard does not see those strings.

## Key Entry Points

- App startup: `src/OrcaSlicer.cpp`
- Slicing pipeline: `src/libslic3r/Print.cpp`
- All print/printer/material settings: `src/libslic3r/PrintConfig.cpp`
- GUI: `src/slic3r/GUI/`
- Core algorithms: `src/libslic3r/` (GCode/, Fill/, Support/, Geometry/, Format/, Arachne/)
- Printer profiles: `resources/profiles/[manufacturer].json`

## JusPrin Production UI

- Start with `agent-docs/jusprin/README.md` for the canonical product definition, production architecture, verification method, Orca integration guidance, and design system.
- Before editing any file outside `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/`, read `agent-docs/jusprin/fork-stewardship.md`. Every line changed in an OrcaSlicer-owned file is a line this fork re-resolves at every rebase, so those changes must be small, product-neutral, additive where possible, and accompanied by the rebase evidence that document requires.
- Experimental plans, probes, screenshots, logs, and temporary UI code remain on `jusprin-v2-poc`. Use `agent-docs/jusprin/poc-reference.md` for exact commit and path pointers; do not cherry-pick the POC wholesale.
- Curated brand and semantic UI assets live under `resources/jusprin/`.
- Before writing or changing any UI code, native or Agent page, follow "Writing UI code" in `agent-docs/jusprin/design-system.md`: every color, radius, font, and control size comes from the token file through `ShellTheme`, the shell recipes, or the CSS variables. A value with no token gets a token and a guard first, never a literal.
- Temporary working docs (handoffs, findings, plans written for another agent) stay untracked: never commit them, and never add them to `.gitignore` or `.git/info/exclude`. Untracked files in `git status` are how Kenneth tracks work that isn't finished.

## Critical Constraints

- **Backward compatibility required** for .3mf project files and printer profiles
- **Cross-platform** — all changes must work on Windows, macOS, and Linux
- Profile/format changes need version migration handling
- Dependencies built separately in `deps/build/`, then linked to main app

## Code review focus areas

- Changes must not cause regressions in existing functionality, defaults, profiles, or project compatibility.
- Features gated by options must not affect existing behavior when those options are disabled.
- Changes should follow the existing code style and architecture. Architectural changes should be justified in code comments and the PR description.
- Add helper functions or utilities only when existing code cannot reasonably be reused. Avoid duplication.
- Changes to OrcaSlicer-owned files must be additive where possible. Rewriting an upstream function, or reimplementing upstream behavior beside it, needs explicit justification in the PR description.
- When an upstream line is deleted or relocated, say where it went and what a future rebase must carry into the new home.
- Keep code concise and clear. Manually simplify AI generated bloated codes before review.
- Include targeted tests or documented verification for behavior changes, especially in slicing logic, profiles, formats, and GUI defaults.

# Global Claude Code Rules

## How to Communicate

Talk like a colleague explaining something out loud, not like a report.

1. **Full sentences, one idea each.** Lead with a concrete case (someone opens a file, chats twenty times, then runs out of credits) before any general point. Never pack a mechanism into a noun phrase like "hidden fair-use ceiling". Say what the person sees happen, step by step.

## Git Commit Policy

When the user asks to commit changes:

1. Run `git status` and `git diff` to review the changes.
2. If you are confident that both the changes are correct and the proposed commit message accurately describes them, proceed with git commit without asking for confirmation.
3. If you have any uncertainty about either, stop and ask the user for explicit confirmation before committing.

When the user asks to revert or amend commits:
1. Explain what will be reverted/amended
2. Ask for confirmation before executing any `git revert`, `git reset`, or `git commit --amend` commands
3. Only proceed after explicit user approval
4. Never revert commits without explicit user confirmation.

This applies to all git operations that modify commit history.

## Submodule Policy

**Never commit or attempt to commit submodule updates.**

When `git status` shows modified submodules (e.g., `modified: some-submodule (new commits)`):
- Do not stage or commit the submodule change
- Do not include submodules when running `git add`
- Leave submodule management to the user

## Testing Principles

1. Always test your code change unless the change is not testable.

2. If the change is not testable, highlight the reason why it's not testable to get the user's attention.

3. By default, do end-to-end testing on everything that may potentially be impacted by your change on the local dev environment.

4. Search for how the dev environment should be started if it's not obvious.

5. Look for README files in the project for related info.

6. Check if the local dev is already running before you try to start it again.

## Software Engineering Principles

1. **Don't reinvent the wheel (avoid Not Invented Here).** Before building anything, check whether the codebase or the libraries it already uses do it, and reuse that. Re-implementing something is a decision that needs a stated justification.

## Bug Fix Policy

**Never apply a fix for a bug you cannot reproduce.**

Before writing any fix:
1. Reproduce the bug first in the local dev environment.
2. If the bug cannot be reproduced locally (e.g., only manifests in release mode, requires specific device conditions, or the debug framework masks the crash), stop and tell the user — do not apply the fix.
3. A fix is only valid if you can demonstrate the broken behavior before the fix and the correct behavior after.

## Epistemic Discipline — Root Cause of Repeated Errors

**The core failure mode: confusing "generating a plausible explanation" with "knowing the answer."**

Coherent ≠ true. A narrative that feels right because it's internally consistent is not a verified fact.

Rules to follow every time:

1. **Search before asserting, not after being challenged.** The internet is always available. Use it proactively, not reactively as damage control.

2. **Explicitly label inference vs. verified fact.** If it hasn't been confirmed by a source, say "my hypothesis is..." or "I'd expect..." — never state it as fact.

3. **"I don't know yet" is a complete and correct answer.** Saying it is more helpful than fabricating a confident-sounding explanation.

## Problem Definition Before Search

**A well-defined problem statement is more valuable than a clever hypothesis.**

The discipline:
1. **Define the problem precisely first.** Strip out assumptions one by one until the statement contains only what is actually known. Remove irrelevant context (e.g. subscription type if it doesn't affect the symptom).
2. **Search for the problem directly** — not for your hypothesis. People who already solved the same problem will surface the real root cause.
3. **Let the search results form the conclusion.** Don't search to confirm what you already believe.
4. **Be flexible about scope.** Start with the most likely affected area (e.g. Discord) but stay open to other channels or systems being equally or more affected.

Searching to validate a hypothesis finds confirmation of whatever you already believed. Searching for the problem finds answers.

## Upstream vs. fork attribution

This checkout holds two codebases: upstream OrcaSlicer (the `upstream` remote, SoftFever/OrcaSlicer) and the JusPrin fork's changes on top of it. Fork changes include everything under `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/` and the seams the fork added inside OrcaSlicer-owned files.

- Say "OrcaSlicer does X" only for behavior upstream ships. Behavior added by a fork commit is "JusPrin does X", even when it lives in an OrcaSlicer-owned file.
- Check before attributing; the file path is not enough. Run `git blame` on the line, then `git branch -r --contains <sha> 'upstream/*'`. No upstream branch containing the commit means the fork owns it. Run `git fetch upstream` first if the remote may be stale.
- If you have not checked, say it is unverified whether the behavior is upstream or fork.

## Error handling discipline

- Do not catch an error merely because it can be caught. Catch only when the code can recover, translate the error at an abstraction boundary, or add context that is essential for diagnosis. Logging alone is not recovery.
- Represent expected states with normal control flow, not exceptions.
- Never turn an invariant violation or an "impossible" state into success or a silent no-op. Fix the invalid transition at the layer that owns the decision and let unexpected failures propagate to Sentry.
- Avoid duplicating defensive checks across layers. Keep lower-level operations strict, with their preconditions enforced by the caller that owns the workflow.
- If concurrency makes an invalid state reachable, fix the ordering or synchronization instead of suppressing the resulting error.
- Suppress an error only when it is genuinely expected and safely recoverable; document the reason and cover it with a test. Never broadly swallow unexpected errors.
- Prefer removing the root cause over reducing the visibility of its symptoms. Tests should encode valid transitions and assert that invalid ones remain visible.

### Building on a shared machine

Several agent sessions build on the same Mac at once. Without a limit, ninja runs one compile job per core plus two, so every build you start can take the whole machine. In 2026-10 one session stacked four builds in one build directory: 56 clang processes on 12 cores. It kept restarting its build to change targets and never limited the job count.

- Before starting a build, check `uptime` and `pgrep -fl ninja`. If the load is already above the core count, wait or build less.
- Limit jobs: `cmake --build … -- -j4`.
- Decide the full target list before starting. Never restart a running build to add or change targets: let it finish, then build the rest.
- Run one build per build directory. Two ninja processes in one directory compete and can leave its records inconsistent.
- Stopping a build means stopping ninja. `pkill -f "cmake --build …"` kills only the cmake wrapper, and ninja keeps compiling. Start long builds in their own process group (`perl -e 'setpgrp(0,0); exec @ARGV' cmake --build …`) and stop them with `kill -- -<pgid>`. Then confirm with `pgrep -fl ninja` before building again.
- When a build is slow, count your own compile processes before blaming the load on other sessions.
- Reuse an existing build where the task allows. Ask before configuring a fresh full-app build the task does not require.

     - The user rejected a two-question model as over-engineered and wanted ONE intuitive status.

     - So the task is a field × connection-type table giving each field's condition to show. The method: research the code and each printer API, then aggregate, as was done for the status table.

2. **Key Technical Concepts**
   - JusPrin is a fork of OrcaSlicer (C++/wxWidgets). The Home page is React (`HomeUI`) in a web view.
   - `HomeSnapshot`'s `PrinterEntry` has `PrinterState {Idle, Printing, Offline}`, defaulting to Idle, and `ConnectionState`.
   - `OrcaHomeBackend` builds the cards; `describe_device` handles Bambu.
   - `HostLaneReader` / `HostLanes`: after f8a1476539 it checks every print host. Moonraker uses its API; any other host counts as answering on any HTTP reply. Poll every 10 s, a reading stays fresh for 30 s.
   - Bambu data comes from `MachineObject` over MQTT. `is_in_printing_status` covers PAUSE, RUNNING, SLICING and PREPARE.
   - Upstream's `MoonrakerPrinterAgent` status stream is switched off with `#if 0`.
   - Design canvas: a Claude artifact of the Design type.
     - Boards are `project/*.dc.html`; the index is `project/canvas.json`.
     - Shared components are pulled in with `<dc-import>`.
     - Tokens live in `project/ds/jusprin/tokens.css`.
     - Local render: `render_dc.py` in `~/.claude/projects/-Users-kenneth-Projects-JusPrin/figma-mirror/tools/composer/`.
   - Memory rules for the canvas:

     - Stop the comment watch after each publish.
     - Do a plain `read` before publishing.

     - `Home/OrcaHomeBackend.cpp:140-167`: `describe_device`, Bambu only.

     - Correct examples elsewhere:

       - `Shell/PrinterMenu.cpp:152` carries a warning comment about this case.
       - The agent's printer list leaves activity empty for a host.
   - **New bug from f8a1476539:** `Shell/SetupCommands.cpp:289` maps a print host that merely answers (`HostLink::Reachable`) to `ConnectionState::Idle` in the header menu. That is the same class of bug.
   - **Reports:**

     - Work folder `scratchpad/work-printer-status/` holds `project/` (copied from the live canvas) and `runtime/dc-runtime.js`.
     - Functions:

     - **Facts line:** host type is never sent to the page. A host's address shows only while Connected. Bambu IP is available but not shown. Nozzle comes from the profile, or from the Bambu reading while online.
     - **Loaded:** Bambu and Moonraker only. Creality and Snapmaker agents exist upstream but are unused.
     - **History:** prints come from Bambu only, so hosts show "Sent N times" at best.
     - **Button:**

---
name: printer-status-one-list-boards
description: "2026-11-04 printer card status proposal: Kenneth rejected a two-question model, asked for one intuitive status; boards on the canvas Main Page, builder in scratchpad."
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: project

On 2026-11-04 Kenneth rejected a two-part printer status (reachability plus activity) as over-engineered: "Let's do just one status… users can intuitively understand." He also said busy and printing are the same to users, and that a not-connected card needs a way to tell whether that is expected (powered off) or to troubleshoot.

# Printer states across connection types

Written 2026-11-04. Sections 1 and 2 describe what exists today. Sections 3 to 5 are a proposal that Kenneth has not agreed to.

## 1. What the app reads today, per connection type (verified in code)

| Connection | Print state | Progress / job | Error | Filament loaded | Is it answering? |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Bambu, LAN or cloud (the Bambu plug-in, over MQTT) | Read. The Home card treats PAUSE, PREPARE and SLICING as "Printing", and FINISH and FAILED as "Idle" (`DeviceManager.cpp:2301`) | Read | Upstream reads it; JusPrin ignores it | Read (AMS and the external spool) | A push within the last 30 s |
| Moonraker (Klipper), through JusPrin's own 10 s poll | Not read | Not read | Not read | Read (`lane_data` or `mmu`) | Read (a reply in the last 30 s) |
| Moonraker, through upstream's printer agent (Qidi, Snapmaker, Creality and OpenEYE profiles) | Code exists but is switched off with `#if 0` upstream, under "disable websocket for now" (`MoonrakerPrinterAgent.cpp:2084`) | Same: switched off | Always 0 | Read only during upstream's filament sync | `/server/info` once, at connect |
| OctoPrint, PrusaLink, PrusaConnect | Not read | Not read | Not read | Not read | Only when someone presses Test |
| Duet, Repetier, MKS, ESP3D, FlashAir, AstroBox, CrealityPrint, Obico, SimplyPrint, ElegooLink, Flashforge, 3DPrinterOS | Not read | Not read | Not read | Flashforge: in upstream dialogs only | Upstream's Test button only; JusPrin's setup calls them "unavailable" |

What the Home card shows today as a result:
- A Bambu card has a real state, but a paused printer reads "Printing", and a failed print reads "Idle".
- Every other card reads "Idle", because that is the state field's starting value. A Moonraker card says whether the host answers. Every other host card says "Connected · address", based only on an address being saved.

## 2. What each printer's own API can report (from its docs or source; "?" = not confirmed)

| API | Ready | Busy (heating, homing, calibrating) | Printing | Paused | Finished / cancelled | Error or needs attention | Controller down while the host still answers | Progress, job name | Filament lanes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Bambu MQTT | IDLE | PREPARE, SLICING, `stg_cur` | RUNNING | PAUSE | FINISH; cancel is FAILED + error 50348044 | FAILED, HMS | no such state | yes | AMS |
| Moonraker / Klipper | `print_stats` standby | `idle_timeout` Printing while standby | printing | paused | complete, cancelled | `print_stats` error | `klippy_state` shutdown, error, disconnected | yes; no time left | `mmu`, `lane_data` (sensor only in core Klipper) |
| OctoPrint (also Obico, AstroBox?) | ready | Starting, Finishing, Cancelling, Pausing | printing | paused | events only (`PrintDone`, `PrintCancelled`) | error | `closedOrError`, HTTP 409 | yes | no |
| PrusaLink / Prusa Connect | IDLE, READY | BUSY | PRINTING | PAUSED | FINISHED, STOPPED | ERROR, ATTENTION | no | yes | MMU3 in Connect |
| Duet | idle | busy, changingTool, starting, updating, pausing, resuming, cancelling | processing (older firmware: printing) | paused | no | ? | halted, off, disconnected | ? | ? |
| Flashforge | ready | busy, heating, calibrate_doing, downloading, pausing, canceling | printing | pause | completed, cancel | error | no | yes | AD5X slots |
| Elegoo (Centauri Carbon) | 0 | homing, leveling, preheating | 13 | 6 | 9, 8 | 14 | no | yes | CC2 only |
| Creality K1/K2 (port 9999) | derived | self-test | state 1 | state 5 | progress 100, state 4 | `err.errcode` | no | yes | CFS ? |
| Repetier, MKS, ESP3D, FlashAir, SimplyPrint, 3DPrinterOS | mostly ? or nothing | | | | | | | | |

## 3. Proposed states (proposal)

The card answers two separate questions. Today one field mixes them up.

**Can the app reach it?**
- **Not connected.** No connection is saved.
- **Checking.** The app has asked and has no answer yet.
- **Live.** It answered within the last 30 seconds.
- **Lost.** It answered before and is silent now.
- **Not checked.** An address is saved, but the app never polls this connection type. This replaces today's green "Connected" for OctoPrint and the others.

**What is the printer doing?** This is filled in only while the connection is Live and the connection type reports it. Otherwise it is Unknown, and the card says nothing about activity.
- **Unknown.** This is the starting value.
- **Ready.** Nothing is running, and a job can start.
- **Busy.** The printer is doing something that is not yet a job, such as heating, homing, leveling, self-test or a file transfer.
- **Printing.** Progress, job name and time left come along when the printer reports them.
- **Paused.**
- **Needs attention.** An error the person must deal with. The printer's own message goes with it.
- **Controller down.** The host answers but the printer controller doesn't, for example Klipper shut down or OctoPrint with its serial port closed.

The last job's outcome (finished, cancelled or failed) is an extra fact on Ready, not a state of its own. Two reasons. OctoPrint reports these only as one-time events. And Bambu and Klipper keep saying FINISH, FAILED or "error" after a print even though the printer is ready to go again. My inference, not confirmed: Prusa's FINISHED behaves the same way.

## 4. Proposed mapping (proposal)

| Connection | Ready | Busy | Printing | Paused | Needs attention | Controller down | Lost |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Bambu | IDLE, FINISH, FAILED with no serious HMS | PREPARE, SLICING | RUNNING | PAUSE | serious or fatal HMS, or `print_error` while paused | n/a | no push for 30 s |
| Moonraker | webhooks ready + `print_stats` standby, complete, cancelled or error | standby while `idle_timeout` is Printing; webhooks startup | printing | paused | ? (a print that errors drops back to Ready with "failed") | `klippy_state` shutdown, error or disconnected | request fails |
| OctoPrint | ready | Starting, Finishing, Cancelling, Pausing | printing | paused | error | `closedOrError` / 409 | request fails |
| PrusaLink | IDLE, READY, FINISHED, STOPPED | BUSY | PRINTING | PAUSED | ERROR, ATTENTION | n/a | request fails |
| Duet | idle | busy and the other transitional values | processing / printing | paused | ? | halted, off, disconnected | request fails |
| Flashforge | ready, completed, cancel | busy, heating, calibrate_doing, downloading | printing | pause | error | n/a | request fails |
| Every other host | Unknown | | | | | | Not checked |

## 5. What it would take, cheapest first (proposal)

1. **Make "Unknown" the starting state and add "Not checked".** No card claims an activity or a connection it didn't read. This covers every connection type at once, and it only touches JusPrin-owned files.
2. **Read Moonraker activity in the poll that already runs every 10 s.** Add one call, `printer/objects/query?webhooks&print_stats&idle_timeout&virtual_sdcard`. That covers Klipper, and should also cover Qidi and Snapmaker U1 if they use the same API (not confirmed). Only JusPrin-owned files change. The other route is switching on upstream's disabled stream, but that edits an upstream file and also turns on upstream's Device-tab behavior, which upstream switched off on purpose.
3. **Read Bambu's Paused, Busy and Needs-attention states** from fields upstream already parses. Only JusPrin-owned files change.
4. **OctoPrint and PrusaLink** would each need a new poll. Later.

Still open:
- I haven't checked whether upstream's Moonraker agent also adds a second, always-Offline device card on Home.
- Whether Prusa's FINISHED is ready for the next job.
- Duet's progress fields.

Kenneth's real Moonraker printer for live tests is `http://raspberrypi.local/` (192.168.0.189 on 2026-11-04). Mainsail there passes requests on to Moonraker, and Moonraker trusts his Mac, so it connects with no API key. My subnet port scan for 7125 that day missed it and found only the Docker hosts on his Mac (`jp-moonraker` on 7125 needs a key; `jp-moonraker-open` on 7126; Mainsail on 8081, which does not pass requests on, and on 8082, which does). Ask Kenneth or try `raspberrypi.local` rather than trusting a scan.

Live chat runs on 2026-11-04 (scratch app copy + copied data folder, GPT-5.4 Mini) found that both times the agent said "you can send prints" after a verified connection, and a generic Klipper printer kept the 250 × 250 bed. Kenneth said "Not now" to fixes. See [[connection-skill-per-connection-type]], [[ux-walkthrough-real-app-recipe]].

- Explore: Read-only search agent for broad fan-out searches — when answering means sweeping many files, directories, or naming conventions and you only need the conclusion, not the file dumps. - statusline-setup: Use this agent to configure the user's Claude Code status line setting. (Tools: Read, Edit)

- linkedin-comment: Generate LinkedIn comments in Kenny's authentic voice - brief, technically specific, casual, honest

- obico-gmail: Access and operate Kenny's shared Obico Gmail account (k@obico.io) with the gog CLI. Use whenever a workflow needs to search, read, draft, reply, send, archive, trash, or deduplicate Obico email, including mail forwarded from addresses such as support@whisprnotes.app. Do not use for unrelated Gmail accounts.
- plain_english: Write output for a generalist full-stack engineer who has no access to the current session context. Use for cold-reader summaries, status updates, task notes, commit messages, and PR descriptions.
- whisprnotes-account-ops: Delete a Whispr Notes user account across all three stores — GCS audio blobs, the app Postgres DB (prod-whisprnotes pod), and the Supabase Auth identity — via the account-ops.sh wrapper. Use when asked to delete/remove/purge a Whispr Notes account.
- entire-search: Search Entire checkpoint history and transcripts with `entire search --json`. Use proactively when the user asks about previous work, commits, sessions, prompts, or historical context in this repository.
- figma-agent-design: Retired 2026-10-20: JusPrin design no longer happens in Figma, which is out of date. Do not use this skill to design in Figma. JusPrin design work happens in the two Claude design artifacts (the Design System and the JusPrin v2 canvas); see agent-docs/jusprin/design-system.md, Writing UI code, rule 5.
- commit-push-pr: Commit, push, and open a PR
- dedupe: Find duplicate GitHub issues
- oncall-triage: Triage GitHub issues and label critical ones for oncall
- cowork-plugin-management:cowork-plugin-customizer: Customize a Claude Code plugin for a specific organization's tools and workflows. Use when: customize plugin, set up plugin, configure plugin, tailor plugin, adjust plugin settings, customize plugin connectors, customize plugin skill, tweak plugin, modify plugin configuration.
- cowork-plugin-management:create-cowork-plugin: Guide users through creating a new plugin from scratch in a cowork session. Use when users want to create a plugin, build a plugin, make a new plugin, develop a plugin, scaffold a plugin, start a plugin from scratch, or design a plugin. This skill requires Cowork mode with access to the outputs directory for delivering the final .plugin file.
- anthropic-skills:built-in-browser: Read this skill before the first step that uses the built-in browser, the browser pane inside the Claude desktop app (also called the in-app browser, the browser pane, Claude's browser, or "your own browser"), whose tools are named mcp__Claude_Browser__* when the session runs in the desktop app and mcp__remote-devices__Claude_Browser__* when a cloud session is linked to the person's computer; before those tools are turned on there may be a single enable__mcp__remote-devices__Claude_Browser tool instead. It covers the pane's persistent sign-ins, tabs and preview_start, reading pages as text, site approvals, what the pane cannot open, and what to do when it cannot be reached. It is not for Claude in Chrome (mcp__claude-in-chrome__* tools), which has its own skill, and it does not decide which browser to use.
- anthropic-skills:chrome-browser: Read this skill before the first step that uses Claude in Chrome, the browser extension whose tools are named mcp__claude-in-chrome__* (also called Chrome, the browser extension, or the external browser) and which acts in the person's real Chrome with their own sign-ins; before those tools are turned on there may be a single enable__mcp__claude-in-chrome tool instead. It covers loading the tools in one ToolSearch call, checking the person's open tabs and working in a new tab, site permissions, GIF recordings, console logs, dialogs to avoid, and when to stop and ask. It is not for the built-in browser (mcp__Claude_Browser__* or mcp__remote-devices__Claude_Browser__* tools), which has its own skill, and it does not decide which browser to use.
- anthropic-skills:computer-use: Read this skill before the first step of any request to do something in an app on the person's own computer (Notes, Finder, System Settings, any desktop app), to look at their screen, or for "computer use". Computer use (desktop control) lets Claude take screenshots of the person's desktop and control it with clicks, typing and scrolling through the Claude desktop app; its tools are named mcp__computer-use__* when the session runs in the desktop app and mcp__remote-devices__computer_* when a cloud session is linked to the person's computer; before computer use is turned on for a conversation there may be no such tools, only an enable__mcp__remote-devices__computer tool, which turns it on. It covers turning it on, picking the right tool, the access flow, and the safety rules for tiered apps, links and financial actions. It is not for websites, which go through Claude in Chrome or the built-in browser and their own skills.
- anthropic-skills:consolidate-memory: Reflective pass over your memory files — merge duplicates, fix stale facts, prune the index.
- anthropic-skills:deep-research: Use this skill when the user's prompt requires (1) researching a topic across multiple sources, comparing options or alternatives, analyzing trends or history, understanding markets or industries, or reviewing literature or studies and (2) synthesizing that research into a comprehensive, narrative report. If you're planning to search the web or internal knowledge bases, consider using this skill. This skill coordinates research subagents, so use it only when you have a tool for spawning subagents (the Agent or Task tool); otherwise, research the question directly.
- anthropic-skills:docs: docs (editable docs people share and comment on; the default for any document, named as a doc or not: a document, report, proposal, resume, cover letter, letter, contract, policy, form, template, worksheet, essay, handbook, guide, how-to, cheat sheet, SOP or other writing to keep, share, collaborate on, send, submit, print or sign; a doc exports to Word, PDF, Markdown or Google Docs, so needing a file to send, attach, upload, submit or print is no reason to pick Word, and a file nobody asked for is a doc, not Word; a plan, comparison, summary or notes asked in chat stays in chat; a pasted claude.ai artifact link may be a doc: check with docs tools first; Word or another file format named, tracked changes wanted, or a .docx to change or use as a template → that format's skill): making one → if no docs-connector instructions are in context, call its `guide` (topic.instructions) first; then create the doc (headings only, no body) before any search, file read or plan, even with files attached.
- anthropic-skills:docx: Use this skill whenever the user wants to create, read, edit, or manipulate Word documents (.docx) or Word templates (.dotx). Triggers include: any mention of Microsoft Word Documents, such as 'Word doc', 'word document', '.docx', '.dotx', 'microsoft doc'. Also use when extracting or reorganizing content from .docx or .dotx files, inserting or replacing images in documents, find-and-replace in Word files, working with tracked changes or comments, or converting content into a polished Word document. If the user asks for a deliverable as a Word or .docx file (to download, email or print), use this skill. However, if they ask for a document, page, report, memo, or notes WITHOUT naming a file format and the session offers Claude's own dedicated document or page skill or connector, use that instead, even if they will email or print it. Do NOT use for PDFs, spreadsheets, Google Docs, or coding unrelated to document generation.
- anthropic-skills:explain-usage: Explain where this session's tokens went, with one simple chart in plain language. Use when the user says things like "explain my usage", "where did my tokens go", or asks for a usage breakdown.
- anthropic-skills:google-workspace: Read this before the first Google Drive, Docs, Sheets or Slides connector call whenever the task creates or changes a Google file. Use this skill whenever the user wants to create or change a Google Doc, Sheet or Slides file in their Google Drive. Triggers include: a request that names Google Docs, Sheets, Slides or Drive and asks to make, edit, format, copy or rename a file; a docs.google.com link with a request to change that file, even a one-line fix or suggested edits; and any follow-up change to a Google file from earlier in the chat, even "change it" or "add a tab". You can tell; the app cannot. A "new_task" turn — and any turn where the user names a task and asks you to suggest, split off or make a task or session for it — does not start with the plan: its first message is `mcp__ccd_session__start_session` with `initiation` "offer" and a `title` — nothing else, no prompt or background yet, so the card is up at once. Do not restate the plan as a list in your text. Every turn in which you kept a task list, changed files or ran commands closes with `mcp__ccd_turn__wrap_up`, called when this turn's work is done, before any closing message: it fills the next-step box, and without the call the app has nothing to draw. The box holds a two-or-three-sentence recap of what is now true and where it stands, including what is not done or not verified. When this turn leaves the user a decision to make or a step to take, it also holds one short question, the decision alone with no reason or recommendation and without listing the options the buttons give, plus buttons of one to three words that answer it; a turn with nothing pending sends the recap alone, and the app then draws no box. Your closing message follows the call, the last thing you say this turn: your answer to the user in full, which the box's recap never replaces. Never write it before the call, where it can reach the user cut to a short summary. The call's result says whether the box shows your question: ask in the message only a question it does not show. While Auto-fix is on for the session's PR the app watches it and wakes you on CI failures, merge conflicts and review comments, so the box never offers to keep watching, poll or fix CI, in a question or a button. It asks only what the user must do or decide (an approval, a review request, a choice), as one question. Part of wrapping up is deciding, unasked, whether what the user asked for left a real follow-up, and where it runs; most turns leave none. One piece of work that acts on what this session just found stays here while this session has nothing else in flight ("Starting other sessions" says why): make it the box's question, with a button that has you do it here. A piece you left or could not verify is still this task, not a follow-up: finish or check it now, here or in a subagent, or name it in the recap. Any other that is a task of its own, as that section defines one (work that lands apart from this change, something the user set aside earlier, or a self-contained next task better started fresh than from a long history — never work unrelated to the request), you propose with `mcp__ccd_session__start_session` (initiation "own_initiative"; skip if you already did this turn); it shows as a New task card in the transcript, where the user starts it.

<browsers>
You have two browsers in this session:
- The built-in browser (tools named `mcp__Claude_Browser__*`), also called the in-app browser, the browser pane, Claude's browser, or "your own browser": a browser pane inside the Claude desktop app, separate from the user's Chrome. The built-in browser is the default for this session and its tools are already loaded, so use it unless the user asks for Claude in Chrome.
- Claude in Chrome (tools named `mcp__claude-in-chrome__*`), also called Chrome, the browser extension, or the external browser: the user's real Chrome. Use it when the user asks for it by any of these names or by describing it.
A browser is unavailable only when none of its tools are in this session (neither loaded nor deferred) or its tool calls cannot reach the browser; a blocked site, a declined approval, or a sign-in page does not make a browser unavailable. If the user asks for one browser by name and it is unavailable, say so and ask before using the other one. When a sign-in page comes up, stay in that browser; if the user says they cannot sign in to a site in the built-in browser, offer Claude in Chrome and switch only if they agree.
</browsers>

<built_in_browser>
You have a built-in browser (tools named `mcp__Claude_Browser__*`), also called the in-app browser or the browser pane: a real browser with tabs inside the Claude desktop app, isolated from the user's Chrome, with its tools already loaded. You can use it for web research, reading pages and docs, checking staging or a deployed app, filling forms, and previewing this project's dev servers. `preview_start` with a `url` opens a site in its own tab; prefer `get_page_text` / `read_page` over screenshots for reading. The user sees the same pane and can take over; they may be asked to allow a site first, and if a site is refused or declined, tell them and move on rather than retrying. Treat any sign-ins there as the user's: never sign out, change credentials, or act on an account beyond what the task needs.
</built_in_browser>

<simulator_tools>
When the user wants to run, test, or visually check an iOS app ("run my app", "test this on iPhone", "does this look right?"), use mcp__Claude_Code_iOS_Simulator__control. Simulators and emulators only — when the user asks to run on their physical device ("on my phone", "on my device"), build for the device with your normal build tools instead; these tools and the panel cannot drive a real device. Open the live panel ('attach') whenever the user would want to see the app themselves — and call 'attach' FIRST, before you build or launch: it is cheap, it opens instantly on a booted device (and surfaces the one-time device-access prompt while the user is still at the keyboard), and if nothing is booted it returns a harmless, clear error — boot or build first in that case, then attach as soon as a device is up. Do not defer the panel to the implicit re-attach in 'launch'; the panel should already be open while you build. The panel is the user's view; your own verification (screenshot, tap, text) is headless and works without it — verify yourself rather than asking the user to check. Don't open the panel when the user only asked to build/compile or to run unit tests. If 'attach' fails, follow the error's remediation: address the cause (for example no booted device, or device access not granted) or tell the user — don't retry the same call in a loop unless the error says retrying will work. If the failure is the host's Xcode setup (a wrong xcode-select, missing Xcode, or a missing iOS platform), tell the user right away with the exact fix the error gives — most of these fixes need their password, so you cannot run them (the error itself says when a fix is one you can run) — and if you continue by driving the Simulator app with generic screen tools instead, say so explicitly; never switch silently. An app in the iOS Simulator reaches a server on the machine your shell runs on at localhost, with no port forwarding.
