(0, 0) is the frame's top-left corner; an app_screenshot of the window is required first. Mutually exclusive with element_index and target.

element_index.description: Index into the AX summary returned by the last app_screenshot (the [N] prefix on each line). Targets that element's center directly instead of by coordinate. Use when coordinate-based clicking returns unsupported(canvas). Refused if something from another page inside the window (an embedded page, or the page around one) is at that position now, or if the action would go to something else of the same page than that element. Mutually exclusive with coordinate and target.

scale.description: For screenshot and zoom only. tools.name: mcp__computer-use__computer_batch

In this session the tools that each carry out one of this tool's actions (left_click, type, key, scroll, left_click_drag, screenshot, etc.) are not available on their own: a single action is a one-item batch. The app_* tools (app_screenshot, app_click, app_type, app_key, app_batch, etc.) act on granted applications without taking over the screen.

Cancer timeline — NOT ['Charting the battle ahead'], YES ['Laying out the stages']. If you have to ask whether it's serious, it is. Otherwise, have fun — reach for alliteration, puns, personification, wordplay, whatever lands in that language. Playful examples — revenue chart: ['Bribing bars to stand taller', 'Asking Q4 where it went']; kanban: ['Herding cards into columns', 'Dragging, dropping, not stopping'].

---
name: screenshots-to-files-via-page-fixture
description: "computer_batch save_to_disk produced no files (2026-09-23); to get screenshot files for a report, replay the observed host state into the built Agent/Home page under Playwright, which saves PNGs; plus the window-overlap trap when another session runs the harness."
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: 49ad3806-419d-49f2-8833-1578cd5bf2b3
  modified: 2026-09-23T21:16:58.377Z
---

On 2026-09-23 a full live walkthrough of the printer panel was driven with display-scope `computer_batch` (`zoom` + `save_to_disk: true`). Every call returned the image, but no path was reported and a disk-wide search found no file. Do not count on `save_to_disk` for deliverables.

**What worked for files:** the [[fake-host-page-fixture]] recipe under the Playwright MCP. Copy `resources/jusprin/agent/index.html` (and `home/index.html`), inject `window.wx` + a `window.SCENES` table of full `state` payloads, serve with `python3 -m http.server`, open `agent.html?panel=printer`, switch scenes with `browser_evaluate` and save with `browser_take_screenshot` (`scale: device`, `filename` under the repo's `.playwright-mcp/`, the only allowed root; move the PNGs out and `rm -rf .playwright-mcp` afterwards so `git status` stays clean). Real printer pictures come from `resources/profiles/<Vendor>/<Model>_cover.png` as data URLs. The credential card renders from a `toolActivities` entry with `tool: 'printer_connect'`, `correlationId` = an assistant message id, state `pending` (card) or `succeeded` ("Sent"). Chips come from a trailing `Choices: a | b` line. 13 scenes took about 10 minutes and matched the live rendering.

**Window overlap trap:** when another session runs `JusPrinShellHarness --printer-live` in a loop, each run opens a 1200x800 window at the same origin (360,125) on the primary display and takes the front, so display-scope zooms and clicks land on *its* window. Move your own instance by pid with a 20-line Swift AX helper (`AXUIElementCreateApplication(pid)` → `kAXPositionAttribute`) onto the built-in display (bounds start at y=1080 here), then `switch_display "Built-in Retina Display"`. The first display click only focuses the window; click again. `--manual-live-agent` does not enable the fake Bambu printer, so the Bambu connect path is out of reach in manual mode.

**Why:** the walkthrough's evidence would otherwise have been lost, and a click into the other session's scripted run could have corrupted its result.

**How to apply:** for any "take screenshots" request on the web pages, plan on the fixture route for files from the start and use the live app only to observe. See [[live-test-built-app-on-mac]] and [[printer-live-harness-lessons]].

name: fake-host-page-fixture
description: "Render the built AgentUI/HomeUI bundles in the built-in browser with a scripted fake native host, to see page states the live app makes hard to catch"

On 2026-09-23 a full live walkthrough of the printer panel was driven with display-scope `computer_batch` (`zoom` + `save_to_disk: true`). Every call returned the image, but no path was reported and a disk-wide search found no file. Do not count on `save_to_disk` for deliverables.

**What worked for files:** the [[fake-host-page-fixture]] recipe under the Playwright MCP. Copy `resources/jusprin/agent/index.html` (and `home/index.html`), inject `window.wx` + a `window.SCENES` table of full `state` payloads, serve with `python3 -m http.server`, open `agent.html?panel=printer`, switch scenes with `browser_evaluate` and save with `browser_take_screenshot` (`scale: device`, `filename` under the repo's `.playwright-mcp/`, the only allowed root; move the PNGs out and `rm -rf .playwright-mcp` afterwards so `git status` stays clean). Real printer pictures come from `resources/profiles/<Vendor>/<Model>_cover.png` as data URLs. The credential card renders from a `toolActivities` entry with `tool: 'printer_connect'`, `correlationId` = an assistant message id, state `pending` (card) or `succeeded` ("Sent"). Chips come from a trailing `Choices: a | b` line. 13 scenes took about 10 minutes and matched the live rendering.

**Window overlap trap:** when another session runs `JusPrinShellHarness --printer-live` in a loop, each run opens a 1200x800 window at the same origin (360,125) on the primary display and takes the front, so display-scope zooms and clicks land on *its* window. Move your own instance by pid with a 20-line Swift AX helper (`AXUIElementCreateApplication(pid)` → `kAXPositionAttribute`) onto the built-in display (bounds start at y=1080 here), then `switch_display "Built-in Retina Display"`. The first display click only focuses the window; click again. `--manual-live-agent` does not enable the fake Bambu printer, so the Bambu connect path is out of reach in manual mode.

**Why:** the walkthrough's evidence would otherwise have been lost, and a click into the other session's scripted run could have corrupted its result.

**How to apply:** for any "take screenshots" request on the web pages, plan on the fixture route for files from the start and use the live app only to observe. See [[live-test-built-app-on-mac]] and [[printer-live-harness-lessons]].

`jusprin-newui` (the current working branch as of 2026-09-16) carries an in-process fake Bambu printer, landed as two commits: `7acf075aaa` (implementation, 2026-09-08 10:57) and `e04c0d40d3` (docs, 2026-09-08 11:00). Both are `Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>` — done by a Cursor agent on worktree branch `cursor/cd073db7` (created from `a9adaae973`), then cherry-picked onto `jusprin-newui` (parent `367f5703b3`). Operator guide: `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Testing/README.md`.

**Design:** unlike the Moonraker simulator ([[fake-moonraker-printer-sim]], which fakes the wire protocol and lives on a different branch entirely), this keeps a real Bambu Lab **system** preset selected (so `PresetBundle::is_bbl_vendor()` stays true and every Bambu-only UI gate passes) and substitutes only the printer-agent implementation, at the `NetworkAgentFactory` factory level, under id `jusprin-fake-bambu`. Two earlier attempts (`a162493544`, `3c244108b4`, both reverted same day) tried faking a *non-Bambu* agent or patching the header chip directly — both failed because Bambu-only gates rejected them or because it only patched a symptom. Faking Bambu's real network (MQTT/TLS 8883, FTPS 990, discovery) was evaluated and explicitly rejected as out of scope.

**The seam:** exactly 4 added lines in `GUI_App::switch_printer_agent` (`src/slic3r/GUI/GUI_App.cpp:3574-3579`, 1 include + 3 body lines) — inside the existing `if (preset_bundle->is_bbl_vendor())` branch, `fake_bambu_printer_agent_id(app_config)` overrides `effective_agent_id` when fake mode is on, otherwise the branch is untouched. No upstream line deleted.

**Config surface is a JSON file only, no MCP tools** (Kenneth's explicit call): turn it on via `"jusprin": {"fake_printer": true}` in `JusPrin2.conf` (JSON booleans store as the string `"true"`; an INI `[jusprin]` block is silently ignored), then drive live state by writing `<datadir>/jusprin/fake_printer.json` (reread ~1s) with `state`/`progress`/`nozzle`/`bed`/`offline` keys. The C++ parameter carrying the datadir into the agent is misleadingly named `log_dir` (an upstream `NetworkAgentFactory::PrinterAgentFactory` convention, documented as "Directory for log files") — verified it's actually `data_dir()` at the call site, not a log subdirectory; don't be misled by the name when reading the code.

Emulates printer type `N1` (`JUSPRIN_FAKE_BAMBU_PRINTER_TYPE`), device id `FAKE001`, shows as **JusPrin Fake A1 mini (LAN)** in Select Machine. Idle/Printing/Offline is the printer-menu **first row** (opened by clicking the printer half of the chip), never on the chip itself. The heartbeat thread does not start in the constructor — only in `set_queue_on_main_fn` when a real callback is set — so unit tests that never wire that callback stay quiet. Test target: `jusprin_fake_bambu_tests` (`tests/jusprin/test_fake_bambu_agent.cpp`), coexists with `shell_theme_tests` in the same CMakeLists (their merge was a conflict the cherry-pick resolved by keeping both).

Doc pointers added in the two landing commits: `AGENTS.md`, `agent-docs/jusprin/README.md`, `agent-docs/jusprin/engineering-method.md` ("Printer tests without hardware" section), `agent-docs/jusprin/orca-integration-guide.md`. A planning handoff doc (`agent-docs/jusprin/fake-bambu-printer-handoff.md`) was never committed and doesn't exist in the tree — don't look for it.

**Why:** Kenneth wants Bambu-path testing (header menu state, Select Machine, print job) without hardware, on the branch he actually works on day to day — distinct from the Moonraker/Klipper simulator, which stays on `jusprin-newui-fakeprinter` and covers the print-host HTTP path instead.

**How to apply:** For "fake a printer on jusprin-newui" requests, this is the one that's actually there — check `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Testing/` first. See [[verify-current-branch-before-memory-recall]] for why this file exists: an earlier session answered "how do we fake a printer" from the Moonraker memory alone and missed this entirely, because it never grepped the current tree for "fake"/"Testing" before recalling.
# Fake Bambu printer (in-process)

Substitutes `FakeBambuAgent` for Bambu's closed network plugin so header menu,
Select Machine, and print can run without hardware. It is not a network fake:
MQTT, FTPS, and discovery are not implemented.

Moonraker and OctoPrint printers run against the real host software in Docker
([print hosts README](../../../../../tests/printer_hosts/README.md)). Do not
add a Bambu network fake unless asked.

This file is the operator guide for humans and AI agents.

## What success looks like

- Log: `switch_printer_agent: printer agent switched to jusprin-fake-bambu`
- Log: `set_selected_machine=FAKE001` and later `FakeBambuAgent: connected FAKE001`
- Printer chip shows `Bambu Lab A1 mini · 0.4` (nickname and nozzle only)
- Click the **printer** half of that chip. The **first menu row** is Idle,
  Printing, or Offline. Those words are never on the chip itself.

If the log says `moonraker` or `orca`, the fake is not in the path. Stop and
fix the preset; do not patch UI gates.

## Turn it on

Quit JusPrin first. The app rewrites `JusPrin2.conf` on exit.

`JusPrin2.conf` is JSON. Under the scratch datadir:

```json
"jusprin": { "fake_printer": true }
```

JSON `true` is what the app stores; `get("jusprin", "fake_printer")` reads as
the string `"true"`. An INI `[jusprin]` block is ignored.

Keep a **Bambu Lab printer** selected: a real system preset, typically
`Bambu Lab A1 mini 0.4 nozzle`, or a named printer that inherits one.
`is_bbl_vendor()` must be true; it reads the inherited `printer_model`, so
either works. An embedded 3mf preset named
`Bambu Lab A1 mini 0.4 nozzle(Tape_4_3MF.3mf)` is not enough; the agent stays
`orca`.

**Add a printer…** in the printer menu installs the system preset and saves it
as a named printer (a user profile such as `Bambu Lab A1 mini`), which is what
Home lists. Alternatively copy `Resources/profiles/BBL` into
`<datadir>/system/` and add the A1 mini model to the `models` array in
`JusPrin2.conf`, then select the system preset. Opening
`~/Downloads/Tape_4_3MF.3mf` only helps after that vendor is installed.

Launch a **scratch** `--datadir`. Do not point fake mode at the everyday
config. JusPrin turns `single_instance` on at every start; its instance lock
lives in the data directory, so a scratch `--datadir` runs as its own instance
beside another JusPrin. Do not pass `--no-single-instance`; Boost rejects it.

The fake emulates printer type `N1` (A1 mini). Select Machine lists it as
**JusPrin Fake A1 mini (LAN)**.

For an MCP client, the shell harness does all of this in its own datadir:
`shell_integration_harness --manual-mcp <dir> --fake-printer` saves a
**Fake A1 mini** printer, connects it to the fake and selects it before it
prints `HARNESS MCP FIXTURE READY`. Edits to the conf would not survive: the
fixture rewrites it at startup.

## Drive state

Write `<datadir>/jusprin/fake_printer.json` (create `jusprin/` if needed). The
fake rereads it about once a second.

```json
{"state":"printing","progress":0.4,"nozzle":210,"bed":60,"offline":false}
```

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `state` | `idle`, `heating`/`prepare`, `printing`/`running`, `pause`, `finished`, `failed` |
| `progress` | 0–1, mapped to `mc_percent` |
| `nozzle`, `bed` | °C |
| `offline` | `true` stops `push_status`; after ~30 s the menu first row is Offline |
| `spools` | loaded AMS spools; see below. Absent leaves whatever was last set |

# Fake Bambu printer (in-process)

Substitutes `FakeBambuAgent` for Bambu's closed network plugin so header menu,
Select Machine, and print can run without hardware. It is not a network fake:
MQTT, FTPS, and discovery are not implemented.

Moonraker and OctoPrint printers run against the real host software in Docker
([print hosts README](../../../../../tests/printer_hosts/README.md)). Do not
add a Bambu network fake unless asked.

This file is the operator guide for humans and AI agents.

## What success looks like

- Log: `switch_printer_agent: printer agent switched to jusprin-fake-bambu`
- Log: `set_selected_machine=FAKE001` and later `FakeBambuAgent: connected FAKE001`
- Printer chip shows `Bambu Lab A1 mini · 0.4` (nickname and nozzle only)
- Click the **printer** half of that chip. The **first menu row** is Idle,
  Printing, or Offline. Those words are never on the chip itself.

If the log says `moonraker` or `orca`, the fake is not in the path. Stop and
fix the preset; do not patch UI gates.

## Turn it on

Quit JusPrin first. The app rewrites `JusPrin2.conf` on exit.

`JusPrin2.conf` is JSON. Under the scratch datadir:

```json
"jusprin": { "fake_printer": true }
```

JSON `true` is what the app stores; `get("jusprin", "fake_printer")` reads as
the string `"true"`. An INI `[jusprin]` block is ignored.

Keep a **Bambu Lab printer** selected: a real system preset, typically
`Bambu Lab A1 mini 0.4 nozzle`, or a named printer that inherits one.
`is_bbl_vendor()` must be true; it reads the inherited `printer_model`, so
either works. An embedded 3mf preset named
`Bambu Lab A1 mini 0.4 nozzle(Tape_4_3MF.3mf)` is not enough; the agent stays
`orca`.

**Add a printer…** in the printer menu installs the system preset and saves it
as a named printer (a user profile such as `Bambu Lab A1 mini`), which is what
Home lists. Alternatively copy `Resources/profiles/BBL` into
`<datadir>/system/` and add the A1 mini model to the `models` array in
`JusPrin2.conf`, then select the system preset. Opening
`~/Downloads/Tape_4_3MF.3mf` only helps after that vendor is installed.

Launch a **scratch** `--datadir`. Do not point fake mode at the everyday
config. JusPrin turns `single_instance` on at every start; its instance lock
lives in the data directory, so a scratch `--datadir` runs as its own instance
beside another JusPrin. Do not pass `--no-single-instance`; Boost rejects it.

The fake emulates printer type `N1` (A1 mini). Select Machine lists it as
**JusPrin Fake A1 mini (LAN)**.

For an MCP client, the shell harness does all of this in its own datadir:
`shell_integration_harness --manual-mcp <dir> --fake-printer` saves a
**Fake A1 mini** printer, connects it to the fake and selects it before it
prints `HARNESS MCP FIXTURE READY`. Edits to the conf would not survive: the
fixture rewrites it at startup.

## Drive state

Write `<datadir>/jusprin/fake_printer.json` (create `jusprin/` if needed). The
fake rereads it about once a second.

```json
{"state":"printing","progress":0.4,"nozzle":210,"bed":60,"offline":false}
```

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `state` | `idle`, `heating`/`prepare`, `printing`/`running`, `pause`, `finished`, `failed` |
| `progress` | 0–1, mapped to `mc_percent` |
| `nozzle`, `bed` | °C |
| `offline` | `true` stops `push_status`; after ~30 s the menu first row is Offline |
| `spools` | loaded AMS spools; see below. Absent leaves whatever was last set |

No `spools` (or an empty array) reports no AMS at all, same as before this
field existed. A non-empty array reports one AMS unit (id `"0"`) with one
tray per spool, up to 4:

```json
{"spools": [{"subBrands": "PLA Matte", "trayType": "PLA", "colour": "5F7D4FFF"}]}
```

`subBrands` is what `PrinterDiscovery.cpp` reads back as the spool's name
when set (ahead of `trayType`), so it is the field worth setting for a
saved/network-printer card or receipt to show something. `trayType` is the
spool's material (Home's Loaded row names it); the fake sends it beside a
`tray_info_idx`, since upstream ignores a type that arrives without one.
`filamentId` sets that id (`"GFA01"` is Bambu PLA Matte); left out, the
id is empty, and Orca's filament sync skips the tray. `colour` is optional: a spool without it reports no colour, and Home
draws no swatch for it.

Delete the file, or set `"offline": false` and `"state":"idle"`, to return to Idle.

## Print

Slice, then Print (or Cmd+Shift+G on macOS). Send completes without a printer.
The log records `FakeBambuAgent: start_local_print file=...`.

If the control file is present, that file wins: send still succeeds, but the
menu stays on the file's state. Remove the file if you want the canned printing
scenario after send.

## Isolate a running app (agents)

Another JusPrin may already be open. Do not send keys or clicks to it.

On macOS both processes are often named `OrcaSlicer`. Target by unix pid or by
a unique `CFBundleIdentifier` on a ditto'd `.app` (then ad-hoc `codesign`).
`osascript` `unix id` filters can match the wrong process; prefer
`AXUIElementCreateApplication(pid)` or the unique bundle id.

Keyboard events posted to the pid work while the Mac is locked; mouse events
posted that way do not. Menus only open when that app is frontmost. The printer
half of the chip is a wx control (`SetName("Printer")`) and often has no AX
title; click by coordinates after a screenshot, or use the documented shortcut
for Print.

Logs: `<datadir>/log/debug_*.log`. This machine's default `grep` may be ugrep;
use `/usr/bin/grep -a` on app logs.

## A real printer, no model

The printer tools are not exposed over MCP, so `probe.call` cannot reach them.
`shell_integration_harness --printer-network-check <dir> <address> <version>`
drives them with a scripted stand-in for the model, on Bambu's real plug-in:
copy `plugins/` from a data folder that has it into `<dir>` first, and pass the
version in its `libbambu_networking_<version>.dylib` name. It expects a P1S in
cloud mode at `<address>`, prints each tool result and note as
`HARNESS NETWORK` lines, and sends the printer nothing. `--simulate-announce` after
the version hands the app that announcement itself 25 seconds in, for when no
printer is on; it tests everything after the plug-in, not the plug-in. Printers announce on UDP
2021. While another program holds that port the plug-in hears nothing, and
`printer_connection_status` reports `port_taken`, so quit whatever
`lsof -nP -iUDP:2021` names first. The plug-in takes the port only as the app
starts, so once that program lets go the status reports `not_listening` until a
restart. Holding the port from a small script is how to test both states.

`--printer-connect-skill <dir> <address> <version>` runs the same chats for
the connection skill; pass `none` as the version to run without the plug-in.
`--open-issue` after the version also calls `issue_report_open`, which opens
the default browser on a filled-in GitHub issue page. Nothing is filed unless
someone presses Submit there, so close the tab. That run keeps its data
folder; the link is in `log/debug_*.log` under "opening an issue page".

The search confirms the code's meaning but doesn't identify a cause or fix.

- **Meaning:** Bambu's community error-code list maps 0300400C to "Printing was cancelled." The decimal value 50348044 is the same code (0x0300400C), so the two forms refer to one error.
- **Common reports:** Several users in the "Print Cancelled, but why and by what?" forum thread describe the same message on P1-series printers, often on long prints. Some say the printer was still moving when the app reported cancellation. One user suggested making other error-handling instead of the 'cancelled print' error-handling.
- **Suspected causes:** Posters have blamed SD cards, slicer versions, and firmware. One user downgraded their firmware and didn't have the issue again, but others reported it recurring on older firmware. A forum post about an A1 with this code says "I found the code, but not the answer."
- **Support:** Bambu Lab support has responded in that thread, and a user reported opening a ticket with logs and the 3MF file.

No official Bambu explanation or confirmed fix appeared in these results. The most useful next steps are checking the HMS/history log for the events leading up to the cancel, noting firmware and slicer versions, and opening a support ticket with logs.

lines: // Present and an array replaces the loaded spools wholesale, same as
// every other field here; absent leaves whatever the step already had
// rather than clearing it, so a later poll that only touches state or
+    // Bambu's error code for what stopped or paused the job; 0 is none.
// Empty means no AMS reported at all, matching every step before this
// field existed -- the default scenario and presets stay AMS-free.
| `offline` | `true` stops `push_status`; after ~30 s the menu first row is Offline |
| `spools` | loaded AMS spools; see below. Absent leaves whatever was last set |

+| `print_error` | Bambu's error code for what stopped or paused the job, as a decimal number: `117473297` (`0x07008011`, AMS filament ran out) with `"state":"pause"` puts Home's card on Needs attention; `50348044` (`0x0300400C`, "Printing was cancelled") with `"state":"failed"` reads as a cancelled last print. Absent is `0` |
| `send_fails` | `true` makes the next print or storage upload fail as an upload failure (read at the moment of Send), so OrcaSlicer's send dialog shows its error and reports no success |

| `connect_fails` | a code such as `"5"` (or `true`, which is `"5"`) makes every connect report `ConnectStatusFailed` with that code to the app, as the plug-in does for a printer that refuses; upstream reads `"5"` as a wrong access code and erases the saved one. Nothing connects while it is set. Tests can also call `fail_next_connect(code)` on the agent for one connect |

---
name: printer-status-one-list-boards
description: "2026-11-04 printer card status proposal: Kenneth rejected a two-question model, asked for one intuitive status; boards on the canvas Main Page, builder in scratchpad."
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: cf7649d3-46dd-4047-a831-32851ae18292
  modified: 2026-11-05T14:37:33.942Z
---

On 2026-11-04 Kenneth rejected a two-part printer status (reachability plus activity) as over-engineered: "Let's do just one status… users can intuitively understand." He also said busy and printing are the same to users, and that a not-connected card needs a way to tell whether that is expected (powered off) or to troubleshoot.

Proposed single list (not yet agreed): Not connected (reason + "Last connected …" + Reconnect), Ready (with "last print finished/failed" only when the printer says), Printing (includes heating, homing for a job), Paused, Needs attention (printer's message), Connected (reachable, activity not reported), Connecting… (only before the first answer). Klipper shut down / "Lost communication with MCU" maps to Not connected with Klipper's message.

Boards: canvas https://claude.ai/artifact/ENCtdaz7gjynfbcy4JYbWJ version 1793859430-86aa, Main Page, row at y=2960 under the title "Printer card · one status (proposal, 2026-11-04)": `printer-status-01`…`05` (three Home screens, five-printer full vs short-rows comparison, every-status sheet). Kenneth had the camera put back (2026-11-05): 135 px LIVE block on Printing and Paused cards (Bambu, and Klipper when Moonraker lists a webcam). With it the printing card is 412 px vs 265, so even the one-line version scrolls while something prints. Builder: session scratchpad `build_printer_status.py` (lost on restart; the boards are the record).

**Decided by Kenneth, 2026-11-05:** no collapsed or one-line form. "the best design is to determine if each of those fields need to show. And let the card naturally grow or shrink based on how many fields are being shown." Next step he asked for: each card field's condition to show, per connection type, found the way the status table was (code reads + each printer API's docs, then aggregated).

**Field rules** (scratchpad report `printer-card-fields-by-connection.md`, 2026-11-04): each card field has one show-condition, the same for every printer; the connection type only decides if a value exists. **Kenneth, 2026-11-05:** camera "always on as long as the stream is available" (not only while printing or paused); build order "Moonraker, then bambu" (Moonraker activity/job/message/camera in the existing 10 s poll first, then Bambu fields already in MachineObject).

**Why:** the card said "Idle" for a Moonraker printer whose Klipper was shut down; root cause was a state field defaulting to Idle that only Bambu sets.

**How to apply:** the short-rows board (printer-status-05) is the rejected option; draw cards that grow and shrink by field. Don't build until the field conditions are agreed; see [[kenneth-real-moonraker-raspberrypi-local]].

content.text:
Home's printer cards now show what each Klipper or Bambu printer reports instead of a bare "Idle". Each card has its status, the job, the percent and time left, the printer's own message, when it was last connected, and how the last print ended. A Klipper card shows its camera whenever the camera answers, as you asked. Nothing is committed.

**What I tested**

- **Klipper:** I ran the app on the Docker test printer and stepped it through each state. The cards read:
  - Printing: "Printing · 4% · 14m left", with the job name.
  - Paused: "Paused · at 5%".
  - Ended: "Ready · last print cancelled" or "Ready · last print finished".
  - Board shut down: "Klipper stopped: Lost communication with MCU 'mcu'".
  - Klipper stopped: "Klipper isn't running."
  - Pi off: "127.0.0.1:7130 isn't answering." with Reconnect.
  - The extra "127.0.0.1:7130" card that used to sit beside the named printer is gone.
- **Bambu:** I tested against the fake Bambu printer, in six new harness checks. They all pass.
  - A printer that pauses on an error reads "Needs attention" with Bambu's message for the error.
  - A pause without an error reads "Paused".
  - A printing card names the job.
  - After a print ends, the card says whether it finished, failed or was cancelled.
- **Automated tests:**
  - Native tests: 200 pass.
  - Home page tests: 123 pass.
  - Fake Bambu printer tests: 14 pass.
  - Every print-host and Home card check in the shell harness passes.

**Problems found while testing, now fixed**

- **Frozen camera:** In the app's web view, a camera stream that stops raises no error. The image just keeps its last frame, still labelled LIVE; I watched it do this for 30 seconds. The card now asks the camera for one picture every 5 seconds. The camera comes off the card about 6 seconds after it stops, and comes back with the stream reconnected about 5 seconds after it returns.
- **"Last connected just now":** This showed on a printer whose Klipper had been down for minutes, because the Pi kept answering. It now gives the last time Klipper itself was up.
- **Cut-off facts line:** The line with the connection type, address and model was cut off with "…", which hid the model and nozzle. It now wraps.

**Still open**

- **Bambu camera:** Bambu printers don't offer a camera address the page can show. Upstream plays their cameras through its own native player, so Bambu cards have no camera yet. The question box asks whether to build a native bridge for them now.
- **Harness failures outside this change:**
  - The harness's printer-setup run stops early on a nozzle-panel check, at a project folder that doesn't exist. I skipped that section temporarily to reach the printer checks, then put the file back exactly as it was.
  - Three checks also fail because closing the setup panel during a connection test still saves the late answer.
  - My change doesn't touch either code path, but I haven't run them against an unchanged build to prove they failed before.
- **Design System artifact:** The new design token, a camera height of 135, still needs adding there.

I sent a picture of the real Home page drawing five of these cards.

Sources for the Bambu cancel code (0300400C means "Printing was cancelled"): [Bambu forum, error code list](https://forum.bambulab.com/t/poll-bambu-lab-please-provide-a-complete-list-of-error-codes/17232/7), [Bambu forum, 0300-400C](https://forum.bambulab.com/t/printing-was-cancelled-0300-400c-1330/88015/3). On camera streams freezing without an error: [Stack Overflow, detecting when an MJPEG stream stops](https://kiwix.lema.org/stackoverflow.com_en_all_2023-11/questions/67204268/how-to-detect-when-mjpeg-stream-stops-with-javascript).

# Global Claude Code Rules

## How to Communicate

Talk like a colleague explaining something out loud, not like a report.

1. **Full sentences, one idea each.** Lead with a concrete case (someone opens a file, chats twenty times, then runs out of credits) before any general point. Never pack a mechanism into a noun phrase like "hidden fair-use ceiling". Say what the person sees happen, step by step.

2. **No labels of your own.** Names you made up while working ("phase 2", "board 6a", "the M4 batch", "the three decisions") mean nothing to me. Name a thing by what it is or does. To ask about a screen, say where it is and send the picture.

3. **Ask decisions in full, as questions.** Start with "Decision needed". Give one paragraph per decision: what it is, why it's mine, the options with what each costs, and your pick. End it with a "?". Never refer to a decision by a label, a count, or the report it's in. Don't hand me a choice you could settle yourself by searching or measuring.

4. **Mark proposals as proposals.** Keep apart what the code does today, what you propose, and what I have agreed to. Never write an idea I haven't approved as if it were settled. Before calling something "my rule", find my actual words.

5. **Report outcomes, not the journey.** Leave out problems you hit and solved unless they change what I do next. For an investigation, say what the problem was, how you solved it, what you tested and the result, and what's still open. Keep it under about 500 words.

## Git Commit Policy

When the user asks to commit changes:

1. Run `git status` and `git diff` to review the changes.
2. If you are confident that both the changes are correct and the proposed commit message accurately describes them, proceed with git commit without asking for confirmation.
3. If you have any uncertainty about either, stop and ask the user for explicit confirmation before committing.

When the user asks to revert or amend commits:
1. Explain what will be reverted/amended
2. Ask for confirmation before executing any `git revert`, `git reset`, or `git commit --amend` commands
3. Only proceed after explicit user approval
4. Never revert commits without explicit user confirmation.

This applies to all git operations that modify commit history.

## Submodule Policy

**Never commit or attempt to commit submodule updates.**

When `git status` shows modified submodules (e.g., `modified: some-submodule (new commits)`):
- Do not stage or commit the submodule change
- Do not include submodules when running `git add`
- Leave submodule management to the user

## Testing Principles

1. Always test your code change unless the change is not testable.

2. If the change is not testable, highlight the reason why it's not testable to get the user's attention.

3. By default, do end-to-end testing on everything that may potentially be impacted by your change on the local dev environment.

4. Search for how the dev environment should be started if it's not obvious.

5. Look for README files in the project for related info.

6. Check if the local dev is already running before you try to start it again.

## Software Engineering Principles

1. **Don't reinvent the wheel (avoid Not Invented Here).** Before building anything, check whether the codebase or the libraries it already uses do it, and reuse that. Re-implementing something is a decision that needs a stated justification.

## Bug Fix Policy

**Never apply a fix for a bug you cannot reproduce.**

Before writing any fix:
1. Reproduce the bug first in the local dev environment.
2. If the bug cannot be reproduced locally (e.g., only manifests in release mode, requires specific device conditions, or the debug framework masks the crash), stop and tell the user — do not apply the fix.
3. A fix is only valid if you can demonstrate the broken behavior before the fix and the correct behavior after.

## Epistemic Discipline — Root Cause of Repeated Errors

**The core failure mode: confusing "generating a plausible explanation" with "knowing the answer."**

Coherent ≠ true. A narrative that feels right because it's internally consistent is not a verified fact.

Rules to follow every time:

1. **Search before asserting, not after being challenged.** The internet is always available. Use it proactively, not reactively as damage control.

2. **Explicitly label inference vs. verified fact.** If it hasn't been confirmed by a source, say "my hypothesis is..." or "I'd expect..." — never state it as fact.

3. **"I don't know yet" is a complete and correct answer.** Saying it is more helpful than fabricating a confident-sounding explanation.

## Problem Definition Before Search

**A well-defined problem statement is more valuable than a clever hypothesis.**

The discipline:
1. **Define the problem precisely first.** Strip out assumptions one by one until the statement contains only what is actually known. Remove irrelevant context (e.g. subscription type if it doesn't affect the symptom).
2. **Search for the problem directly** — not for your hypothesis. People who already solved the same problem will surface the real root cause.
3. **Let the search results form the conclusion.** Don't search to confirm what you already believe.
4. **Be flexible about scope.** Start with the most likely affected area (e.g. Discord) but stay open to other channels or systems being equally or more affected.

Searching to validate a hypothesis finds confirmation of whatever you already believed. Searching for the problem finds answers.


## GCP / kubectl Credential Policy

Always use the service account `ai-agent@tsdtechnology.iam.gserviceaccount.com` for all `gcloud` and `kubectl` operations. Before running any such command, switch to it:

```bash
gcloud config set account ai-agent@tsdtechnology.iam.gserviceaccount.com
```

The personal account `k@obico.io` is reserved for the user's own interactive CLI use and its OAuth tokens expire — do not rely on it.

## Sentry Access

- Instance: `sentry.obico.io`
- API base: `https://sentry.obico.io/api/0/`
- Auth token: `REDACTED`
- Usage: `curl -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" <api_url>`

# CLAUDE.md

JusPrin — a long-lived fork of OrcaSlicer (open-source C++17 3D slicer, wxWidgets GUI, CMake build system).

## Upstream vs. fork attribution

This checkout holds two codebases: upstream OrcaSlicer (the `upstream` remote, SoftFever/OrcaSlicer) and the JusPrin fork's changes on top of it. Fork changes include everything under `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/` and the seams the fork added inside OrcaSlicer-owned files.

- Say "OrcaSlicer does X" only for behavior upstream ships. Behavior added by a fork commit is "JusPrin does X", even when it lives in an OrcaSlicer-owned file.
- Check before attributing; the file path is not enough. Run `git blame` on the line, then `git branch -r --contains <sha> 'upstream/*'`. No upstream branch containing the commit means the fork owns it. Run `git fetch upstream` first if the remote may be stale.
- If you have not checked, say it is unverified whether the behavior is upstream or fork.

## Error handling discipline

- Do not catch an error merely because it can be caught. Catch only when the code can recover, translate the error at an abstraction boundary, or add context that is essential for diagnosis. Logging alone is not recovery.
- Represent expected states with normal control flow, not exceptions.
- Never turn an invariant violation or an "impossible" state into success or a silent no-op. Fix the invalid transition at the layer that owns the decision and let unexpected failures propagate to Sentry.
- Avoid duplicating defensive checks across layers. Keep lower-level operations strict, with their preconditions enforced by the caller that owns the workflow.
- If concurrency makes an invalid state reachable, fix the ordering or synchronization instead of suppressing the resulting error.
- Suppress an error only when it is genuinely expected and safely recoverable; document the reason and cover it with a test. Never broadly swallow unexpected errors.
- Prefer removing the root cause over reducing the visibility of its symptoms. Tests should encode valid transitions and assert that invalid ones remain visible.

## Build Commands

```bash
# macOS
cmake --build build/arm64 --config RelWithDebInfo --target all --

# Linux
cmake --build build --config RelWithDebInfo --target all --

# Windows (replace %build_type% with Debug/Release/RelWithDebInfo)
cmake --build . --config %build_type% --target ALL_BUILD -- -m
```

Node/npm is required to build the Agent and Home pages, or configure with `-DJUSPRIN_BUILD_WEB=OFF` and supply the bundles.

### Building on a shared machine

Several agent sessions build on the same Mac at once. Without a limit, ninja runs one compile job per core plus two, so every build you start can take the whole machine. In 2026-10 one session stacked four builds in one build directory: 56 clang processes on 12 cores. It kept restarting its build to change targets and never limited the job count.

- Before starting a build, check `uptime` and `pgrep -fl ninja`. If the load is already above the core count, wait or build less.
- Limit jobs: `cmake --build … -- -j4`.
- Decide the full target list before starting. Never restart a running build to add or change targets: let it finish, then build the rest.
- Run one build per build directory. Two ninja processes in one directory compete and can leave its records inconsistent.
- Stopping a build means stopping ninja. `pkill -f "cmake --build …"` kills only the cmake wrapper, and ninja keeps compiling. Start long builds in their own process group (`perl -e 'setpgrp(0,0); exec @ARGV' cmake --build …`) and stop them with `kill -- -<pgid>`. Then confirm with `pgrep -fl ninja` before building again.
- When a build is slow, count your own compile processes before blaming the load on other sessions.
- Reuse an existing build where the task allows. Ask before configuring a fresh full-app build the task does not require.

## Testing

Catch2 framework. Tests in `tests/` directory.

```bash
cd build && ctest --output-on-failure           # all tests
ctest --test-dir ./tests/libslic3r              # individual suite
ctest --test-dir ./tests/fff_print
```

Printer UI without hardware: `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Testing/README.md` (Bambu in-process fake); Moonraker and OctoPrint: `tests/printer_hosts/README.md` (Docker). Isolated `--datadir`; do not drive another JusPrin instance.

## Code Style

- C++17, selective C++20. PascalCase classes, snake_case functions/variables
- `#pragma once` for headers. Smart pointers and RAII preferred
- Parallelization via TBB — be mindful of shared state
- Wording: a file or object is "opened", "imported", "loaded" or "added", never "arrived". "Arrive" is fine for messages, responses, events and lists. `AgentUI/src/wording.test.ts` guards the text the model reads.
- Wording the model reads calls the product "the app", never Orca or OrcaSlicer: the model speaks as the app, and a second name reads as a second program. `AgentUI/src/wording.test.ts` guards this too. Log lines may name Orca. A throw may only if it never reaches the model: tool results forward save and open errors as they are, and the guard does not see those strings.

## Key Entry Points

- App startup: `src/OrcaSlicer.cpp`
- Slicing pipeline: `src/libslic3r/Print.cpp`
- All print/printer/material settings: `src/libslic3r/PrintConfig.cpp`
- GUI: `src/slic3r/GUI/`
- Core algorithms: `src/libslic3r/` (GCode/, Fill/, Support/, Geometry/, Format/, Arachne/)
- Printer profiles: `resources/profiles/[manufacturer].json`

## JusPrin Production UI

- Start with `agent-docs/jusprin/README.md` for the canonical product definition, production architecture, verification method, Orca integration guidance, and design system.
- Before editing any file outside `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/`, read `agent-docs/jusprin/fork-stewardship.md`. Every line changed in an OrcaSlicer-owned file is a line this fork re-resolves at every rebase, so those changes must be small, product-neutral, additive where possible, and accompanied by the rebase evidence that document requires.
- Experimental plans, probes, screenshots, logs, and temporary UI code remain on `jusprin-v2-poc`. Use `agent-docs/jusprin/poc-reference.md` for exact commit and path pointers; do not cherry-pick the POC wholesale.
- Curated brand and semantic UI assets live under `resources/jusprin/`.
- Before writing or changing any UI code, native or Agent page, follow "Writing UI code" in `agent-docs/jusprin/design-system.md`: every color, radius, font, and control size comes from the token file through `ShellTheme`, the shell recipes, or the CSS variables. A value with no token gets a token and a guard first, never a literal.
- Temporary working docs (handoffs, findings, plans written for another agent) stay untracked: never commit them, and never add them to `.gitignore` or `.git/info/exclude`. Untracked files in `git status` are how Kenneth tracks work that isn't finished.

## Critical Constraints

- **Backward compatibility required** for .3mf project files and printer profiles
- **Cross-platform** — all changes must work on Windows, macOS, and Linux
- Profile/format changes need version migration handling
- Dependencies built separately in `deps/build/`, then linked to main app

## Code review focus areas

- Changes must not cause regressions in existing functionality, defaults, profiles, or project compatibility.
- Features gated by options must not affect existing behavior when those options are disabled.
- Changes should follow the existing code style and architecture. Architectural changes should be justified in code comments and the PR description.
- Add helper functions or utilities only when existing code cannot reasonably be reused. Avoid duplication.
- Changes to OrcaSlicer-owned files must be additive where possible. Rewriting an upstream function, or reimplementing upstream behavior beside it, needs explicit justification in the PR description.
- When an upstream line is deleted or relocated, say where it went and what a future rebase must carry into the new home.
- Keep code concise and clear. Manually simplify AI generated bloated codes before review.
- Include targeted tests or documented verification for behavior changes, especially in slicing logic, profiles, formats, and GUI defaults.

# Global Claude Code Rules

## How to Communicate

Talk like a colleague explaining something out loud, not like a report.

1. **Full sentences, one idea each.** Lead with a concrete case (someone opens a file, chats twenty times, then runs out of credits) before any general point. Never pack a mechanism into a noun phrase like "hidden fair-use ceiling". Say what the person sees happen, step by step.

2. **No labels of your own.** Names you made up while working ("phase 2", "board 6a", "the M4 batch", "the three decisions") mean nothing to me. Name a thing by what it is or does. To ask about a screen, say where it is and send the picture.

3. **Ask decisions in full, as questions.** Start with "Decision needed". Give one paragraph per decision: what it is, why it's mine, the options with what each costs, and your pick. End it with a "?". Never refer to a decision by a label, a count, or the report it's in. Don't hand me a choice you could settle yourself by searching or measuring.

4. **Mark proposals as proposals.** Keep apart what the code does today, what you propose, and what I have agreed to. Never write an idea I haven't approved as if it were settled. Before calling something "my rule", find my actual words.

5. **Report outcomes, not the journey.** Leave out problems you hit and solved unless they change what I do next. For an investigation, say what the problem was, how you solved it, what you tested and the result, and what's still open. Keep it under about 500 words.

## Git Commit Policy

When the user asks to commit changes:

1. Run `git status` and `git diff` to review the changes.
2. If you are confident that both the changes are correct and the proposed commit message accurately describes them, proceed with git commit without asking for confirmation.
3. If you have any uncertainty about either, stop and ask the user for explicit confirmation before committing.

When the user asks to revert or amend commits:
1. Explain what will be reverted/amended
2. Ask for confirmation before executing any `git revert`, `git reset`, or `git commit --amend` commands
3. Only proceed after explicit user approval
4. Never revert commits without explicit user confirmation.

This applies to all git operations that modify commit history.

## Submodule Policy

**Never commit or attempt to commit submodule updates.**

When `git status` shows modified submodules (e.g., `modified: some-submodule (new commits)`):
- Do not stage or commit the submodule change
- Do not include submodules when running `git add`
- Leave submodule management to the user

## Testing Principles

1. Always test your code change unless the change is not testable.

2. If the change is not testable, highlight the reason why it's not testable to get the user's attention.

3. By default, do end-to-end testing on everything that may potentially be impacted by your change on the local dev environment.

4. Search for how the dev environment should be started if it's not obvious.

5. Look for README files in the project for related info.

6. Check if the local dev is already running before you try to start it again.

## Software Engineering Principles

1. **Don't reinvent the wheel (avoid Not Invented Here).** Before building anything, check whether the codebase or the libraries it already uses do it, and reuse that. Re-implementing something is a decision that needs a stated justification.

## Bug Fix Policy

**Never apply a fix for a bug you cannot reproduce.**

Before writing any fix:
1. Reproduce the bug first in the local dev environment.
2. If the bug cannot be reproduced locally (e.g., only manifests in release mode, requires specific device conditions, or the debug framework masks the crash), stop and tell the user — do not apply the fix.
3. A fix is only valid if you can demonstrate the broken behavior before the fix and the correct behavior after.

## Epistemic Discipline — Root Cause of Repeated Errors

**The core failure mode: confusing "generating a plausible explanation" with "knowing the answer."**

Coherent ≠ true. A narrative that feels right because it's internally consistent is not a verified fact.

Rules to follow every time:

1. **Search before asserting, not after being challenged.** The internet is always available. Use it proactively, not reactively as damage control.

2. **Explicitly label inference vs. verified fact.** If it hasn't been confirmed by a source, say "my hypothesis is..." or "I'd expect..." — never state it as fact.

3. **"I don't know yet" is a complete and correct answer.** Saying it is more helpful than fabricating a confident-sounding explanation.

## Problem Definition Before Search

**A well-defined problem statement is more valuable than a clever hypothesis.**

The discipline:
1. **Define the problem precisely first.** Strip out assumptions one by one until the statement contains only what is actually known. Remove irrelevant context (e.g. subscription type if it doesn't affect the symptom).
2. **Search for the problem directly** — not for your hypothesis. People who already solved the same problem will surface the real root cause.
3. **Let the search results form the conclusion.** Don't search to confirm what you already believe.
4. **Be flexible about scope.** Start with the most likely affected area (e.g. Discord) but stay open to other channels or systems being equally or more affected.

Searching to validate a hypothesis finds confirmation of whatever you already believed. Searching for the problem finds answers.

Always use the service account `ai-agent@tsdtechnology.iam.gserviceaccount.com` for all `gcloud` and `kubectl` operations. Before running any such command, switch to it:


# CLAUDE.md

JusPrin — a long-lived fork of OrcaSlicer (open-source C++17 3D slicer, wxWidgets GUI, CMake build system).

## Upstream vs. fork attribution

This checkout holds two codebases: upstream OrcaSlicer (the `upstream` remote, SoftFever/OrcaSlicer) and the JusPrin fork's changes on top of it. Fork changes include everything under `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/` and the seams the fork added inside OrcaSlicer-owned files.

- Say "OrcaSlicer does X" only for behavior upstream ships. Behavior added by a fork commit is "JusPrin does X", even when it lives in an OrcaSlicer-owned file.
- Check before attributing; the file path is not enough. Run `git blame` on the line, then `git branch -r --contains <sha> 'upstream/*'`. No upstream branch containing the commit means the fork owns it. Run `git fetch upstream` first if the remote may be stale.
- If you have not checked, say it is unverified whether the behavior is upstream or fork.

## Error handling discipline

- Do not catch an error merely because it can be caught. Catch only when the code can recover, translate the error at an abstraction boundary, or add context that is essential for diagnosis. Logging alone is not recovery.
- Represent expected states with normal control flow, not exceptions.
- Never turn an invariant violation or an "impossible" state into success or a silent no-op. Fix the invalid transition at the layer that owns the decision and let unexpected failures propagate to Sentry.
- Avoid duplicating defensive checks across layers. Keep lower-level operations strict, with their preconditions enforced by the caller that owns the workflow.
- If concurrency makes an invalid state reachable, fix the ordering or synchronization instead of suppressing the resulting error.
- Suppress an error only when it is genuinely expected and safely recoverable; document the reason and cover it with a test. Never broadly swallow unexpected errors.
- Prefer removing the root cause over reducing the visibility of its symptoms. Tests should encode valid transitions and assert that invalid ones remain visible.

## Build Commands

```bash
# macOS
cmake --build build/arm64 --config RelWithDebInfo --target all --

# Linux
cmake --build build --config RelWithDebInfo --target all --

# Windows (replace %build_type% with Debug/Release/RelWithDebInfo)
cmake --build . --config %build_type% --target ALL_BUILD -- -m
```

Node/npm is required to build the Agent and Home pages, or configure with `-DJUSPRIN_BUILD_WEB=OFF` and supply the bundles.

### Building on a shared machine

Several agent sessions build on the same Mac at once. Without a limit, ninja runs one compile job per core plus two, so every build you start can take the whole machine. In 2026-10 one session stacked four builds in one build directory: 56 clang processes on 12 cores. It kept restarting its build to change targets and never limited the job count.

- Before starting a build, check `uptime` and `pgrep -fl ninja`. If the load is already above the core count, wait or build less.
- Limit jobs: `cmake --build … -- -j4`.
- Decide the full target list before starting. Never restart a running build to add or change targets: let it finish, then build the rest.
- Run one build per build directory. Two ninja processes in one directory compete and can leave its records inconsistent.
- Stopping a build means stopping ninja. `pkill -f "cmake --build …"` kills only the cmake wrapper, and ninja keeps compiling. Start long builds in their own process group (`perl -e 'setpgrp(0,0); exec @ARGV' cmake --build …`) and stop them with `kill -- -<pgid>`. Then confirm with `pgrep -fl ninja` before building again.
- When a build is slow, count your own compile processes before blaming the load on other sessions.
- Reuse an existing build where the task allows. Ask before configuring a fresh full-app build the task does not require.

## Testing

Catch2 framework. Tests in `tests/` directory.

```bash
cd build && ctest --output-on-failure           # all tests
ctest --test-dir ./tests/libslic3r              # individual suite
ctest --test-dir ./tests/fff_print
```

Printer UI without hardware: `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Testing/README.md` (Bambu in-process fake); Moonraker and OctoPrint: `tests/printer_hosts/README.md` (Docker). Isolated `--datadir`; do not drive another JusPrin instance.

## Code Style

- C++17, selective C++20. PascalCase classes, snake_case functions/variables
- `#pragma once` for headers. Smart pointers and RAII preferred
- Parallelization via TBB — be mindful of shared state
- Wording: a file or object is "opened", "imported", "loaded" or "added", never "arrived". "Arrive" is fine for messages, responses, events and lists. `AgentUI/src/wording.test.ts` guards the text the model reads.
- Wording the model reads calls the product "the app", never Orca or OrcaSlicer: the model speaks as the app, and a second name reads as a second program. `AgentUI/src/wording.test.ts` guards this too. Log lines may name Orca. A throw may only if it never reaches the model: tool results forward save and open errors as they are, and the guard does not see those strings.

## Key Entry Points

- App startup: `src/OrcaSlicer.cpp`
- Slicing pipeline: `src/libslic3r/Print.cpp`
- All print/printer/material settings: `src/libslic3r/PrintConfig.cpp`
- GUI: `src/slic3r/GUI/`
- Core algorithms: `src/libslic3r/` (GCode/, Fill/, Support/, Geometry/, Format/, Arachne/)
- Printer profiles: `resources/profiles/[manufacturer].json`

## JusPrin Production UI

- Start with `agent-docs/jusprin/README.md` for the canonical product definition, production architecture, verification method, Orca integration guidance, and design system.
- Before editing any file outside `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/`, read `agent-docs/jusprin/fork-stewardship.md`. Every line changed in an OrcaSlicer-owned file is a line this fork re-resolves at every rebase, so those changes must be small, product-neutral, additive where possible, and accompanied by the rebase evidence that document requires.
- Experimental plans, probes, screenshots, logs, and temporary UI code remain on `jusprin-v2-poc`. Use `agent-docs/jusprin/poc-reference.md` for exact commit and path pointers; do not cherry-pick the POC wholesale.
- Curated brand and semantic UI assets live under `resources/jusprin/`.
- Before writing or changing any UI code, native or Agent page, follow "Writing UI code" in `agent-docs/jusprin/design-system.md`: every color, radius, font, and control size comes from the token file through `ShellTheme`, the shell recipes, or the CSS variables. A value with no token gets a token and a guard first, never a literal.
- Temporary working docs (handoffs, findings, plans written for another agent) stay untracked: never commit them, and never add them to `.gitignore` or `.git/info/exclude`. Untracked files in `git status` are how Kenneth tracks work that isn't finished.

## Critical Constraints

- **Backward compatibility required** for .3mf project files and printer profiles
- **Cross-platform** — all changes must work on Windows, macOS, and Linux
- Profile/format changes need version migration handling
- Dependencies built separately in `deps/build/`, then linked to main app

## Code review focus areas

- Changes must not cause regressions in existing functionality, defaults, profiles, or project compatibility.
- Features gated by options must not affect existing behavior when those options are disabled.
- Changes should follow the existing code style and architecture. Architectural changes should be justified in code comments and the PR description.
- Add helper functions or utilities only when existing code cannot reasonably be reused. Avoid duplication.
- Changes to OrcaSlicer-owned files must be additive where possible. Rewriting an upstream function, or reimplementing upstream behavior beside it, needs explicit justification in the PR description.
- When an upstream line is deleted or relocated, say where it went and what a future rebase must carry into the new home.
- Keep code concise and clear. Manually simplify AI generated bloated codes before review.
- Include targeted tests or documented verification for behavior changes, especially in slicing logic, profiles, formats, and GUI defaults.

And let the card naturally grow or shrink based on how many fields are being shown." Next step he asked for: each card field's condition to show, per connection type, found the way the status table was (code reads + each printer API's docs, then aggregated).

**Built 2026-11-05 (uncommitted on jusprin-newui):** Moonraker poll reads webhooks/print_stats/display_status, history newest job, webcams; Bambu adds job (subtask_name), Needs attention on PAUSE + non-internal print_error (message via HMSQuery, code fallback), last print FINISH/FAILED (0x0300400C = cancelled). Bambu camera NOT built (needs native stream bridge; decision put to Kenneth). Camera check: web view gives no error when an MJPEG stream stops (verified), so the card probes the snapshot every 5 s. "Last connected" = last reading with Klipper up. Fake Bambu control file gained `print_error`. Harness `--printer-setup` dies earlier on an unrelated nozzle-panel `pending` folder error; skip that call temporarily (copy/restore) to reach the printer checks; 3 panel_close_mid_test checks also fail, unrelated, not checked against HEAD.

**Why:** the card said "Idle" for a Moonraker printer whose Klipper was shut down; root cause was a state field defaulting to Idle that only Bambu sets.

**How to apply:** the short-rows board (printer-status-05) is the rejected option; draw cards that grow and shrink by field. Don't build until the field conditions are agreed; see [[kenneth-real-moonraker-raspberrypi-local]].

# When each printer card field shows, by connection type

Written 2026-11-04. Every field has one rule for when it shows, and that rule is the same for every printer. The connection type only decides whether the value exists. Today Bambu fills most of the card. Moonraker fills only the connection and the loaded filament. Every other print host fills only the fields the app keeps itself, plus a bare "Connected".

Sources: the code at jusprin-newui f8a1476539, and each printer API's docs (links in section 3). The rules in section 1 are a proposal Kenneth has not agreed to. Section 2 says what exists today.

## 1. The rule for each field (proposal)

The fields are listed top to bottom, as on the boards.

| Field | Shows when | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Name | Always | |
| ⋯ menu | At least one of settings, rename or remove is allowed | Today an unnamed Bambu LAN printer gets none, so its card has no menu |
| Camera | Status is Printing or Paused, and the app has a stream for this printer | |
| Status word | Always, one of: Printing, Paused, Needs attention, Ready, Connected, Connecting…, Not connected | Comes from the status table already proposed |
| Status detail after the dot | Printing: percent, plus "· 2h 14m left" when time left is known. Paused: "at 27%". Otherwise nothing | |
| Job name | The printer reports a current job (Printing, Paused, or Needs attention during a job) | |
| Progress bar | Same as the job name, and the percent is known | |
| Printer's message | Needs attention: always. Paused: when the printer gives a reason. Not connected: always, giving the reason | When the printer sends only a code, show a sentence with the code. When the app never reached the printer, the reason is the app's own words ("octopi.local isn't answering.") |
| "Last connected …" | Not connected, and the app knows when it last heard from the printer | Hidden when unknown |
| Facts line (connection kind · address · model · nozzle) | Always; each part shows when known | Model and nozzle come from the printer profile for every type, because few printers report them. The address shows for print hosts only |
| Loaded filament | The printer reports what is loaded right now | Never a remembered value on a card that is not connected |
| History link | At least one print or send record exists | The last print's outcome ("last finished Sun") goes here, only when the printer reports it |
| Button | Never set up: "Connect…". Not connected: "Reconnect". Connecting…: none. Otherwise: "Launch monitor" for Bambu, "Open printer window" for a host with a web page | |

## 2. Where each value comes from, per connection type

Key:
- **today**: the card shows it now.
- **in app**: the app already receives it but does not send it to the card.
- **API**: the printer reports it, and the app needs new reading code.
- **calc**: the card has to compute it or look it up.
- **—**: not available.
- **?**: not confirmed.

| Field | Bambu | Moonraker | OctoPrint | PrusaLink | Duet | Flashforge | Elegoo | Creality K | Other hosts* |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Activity part of the status | today, partly (paused reads Printing, failed reads Idle) | API | API | API | API | API | API | API | — |
| Connection part of the status | today | today | today, since f8a1476539 (any HTTP reply) | same | same | same | same | same | same |
| Camera | in app (stream fields; upstream's native player) | API `/server/webcams/list` | API, but the URL is often `localhost` | ? | — | API | API | API | — |
| Job name | in app `subtask_name` | API | API | API | API | API | API | API | — |
| Percent | today | API | API | API | calc | API | API | API | — |
| Time left | today | calc (file estimate minus time printed) | API | API | API | API (freezes while paused) | calc | API | — |
| Printer's message | calc (the app's HMS lookup exists) | API, text | API, text | API, text (ATTENTION has none) | API, text | code only | code only | code only | — |
| Last connected | in app, in memory only | in app, in memory only | in app, in memory only | same | same | same | same | same | same |
| Facts line | in app (connection kind, profile). Nozzle: today | in app (the host type is saved but not sent to the page) | same | same | same | same | same | same | same |
| Loaded filament | today (AMS, external spool) | today (`lane_data` or Happy Hare only) | — | — | API, name only, no colour | API, AD5X only | — | API, CFS only | — |
| Last print outcome | in app `gcode_state` FINISH/FAILED | API history, kept after the job | — (per file only) | API, until the next job | API, kept after the job | ? | API | — (only inferred) | — |
| History | today, prints | today, sends only | today, sends only | same | same | same | same | same | same |

*Other hosts are Prusa Connect, Repetier, MKS, ESP3D, FlashAir, AstroBox, SimplyPrint, Obico and 3DPrinterOS. For SimplyPrint and Obico, "answers" means the company's website answered, not the printer.

"Last connected" is in memory only for every type, so after a restart the line is hidden until the printer is heard again. Saving the time to disk would fix that.

## 3. API sources

- Bambu: OpenBambuAPI [mqtt.md](https://github.com/Doridian/OpenBambuAPI/blob/main/mqtt.md) and [video.md](https://github.com/Doridian/OpenBambuAPI/blob/main/video.md); ha-bambulab [models.py](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/greghesp/ha-bambulab/main/custom_components/bambu_lab/pybambu/models.py).
  - The unit of `mc_remaining_time` is unverified (minutes is assumed).
  - On H2S and H2D, the LAN stream is off until it is switched on at the printer.
- Moonraker: [webcams](https://moonraker.readthedocs.io/en/latest/external_api/webcams/), [history](https://moonraker.readthedocs.io/en/latest/external_api/history/), [file_manager](https://moonraker.readthedocs.io/en/latest/external_api/file_manager/), Klipper [Status Reference](https://www.klipper3d.org/Status_Reference.html).
- OctoPrint: [job](https://docs.octoprint.org/en/master/api/job.html), [printer](https://docs.octoprint.org/en/master/api/printer.html), [settings](https://docs.octoprint.org/en/master/api/settings.html).
- PrusaLink: [OpenAPI spec](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/prusa3d/Prusa-Link-Web/master/spec/openapi.yaml).
  - The camera endpoint on MK4, XL and MINI firmware is unverified.
  - Prusa Connect has no documented public status API.
- Duet: [object model](https://github.com/Duet3D/RepRapFirmware/wiki/Object-Model-Documentation).
- Flashforge: [community docs](https://github.com/Parallel-7/flashforge-api-docs/wiki/HTTP-REST-API).
- Elegoo: [SDCP V3](https://github.com/cbd-tech/SDCP-Smart-Device-Control-Protocol-V3.0.0).
- Creality: [ha_creality_ws](https://github.com/3dg1luk43/ha_creality_ws).

## 4. Problems found on the way (not reproduced, not fixed)

- The header menu calls a print host "Idle" when it only answered (`Shell/SetupCommands.cpp:289`). This is the same kind of bug as the Home card's false "Idle".
- Reconnect on an unnamed Bambu card returns "This printer no longer exists." (`Home/OrcaHomeBackend.cpp:162-166`, `751-753`).
- A print host that is printing reads "Idle" on Home.

- anthropic-skills:built-in-browser: Read this skill before the first step that uses the built-in browser, the browser pane inside the Claude desktop app (also called the in-app browser, the browser pane, Claude's browser, or "your own browser"), whose tools are named mcp__Claude_Browser__* when the session runs in the desktop app and mcp__remote-devices__Claude_Browser__* when a cloud session is linked to the person's computer; before those tools are turned on there may be a single enable__mcp__remote-devices__Claude_Browser tool instead. It covers the pane's persistent sign-ins, tabs and preview_start, reading pages as text, site approvals, what the pane cannot open, and what to do when it cannot be reached. It is not for Claude in Chrome (mcp__claude-in-chrome__* tools), which has its own skill, and it does not decide which browser to use.
- anthropic-skills:chrome-browser: Read this skill before the first step that uses Claude in Chrome, the browser extension whose tools are named mcp__claude-in-chrome__* (also called Chrome, the browser extension, or the external browser) and which acts in the person's real Chrome with their own sign-ins; before those tools are turned on there may be a single enable__mcp__claude-in-chrome tool instead. It covers loading the tools in one ToolSearch call, checking the person's open tabs and working in a new tab, site permissions, GIF recordings, console logs, dialogs to avoid, and when to stop and ask. It is not for the built-in browser (mcp__Claude_Browser__* or mcp__remote-devices__Claude_Browser__* tools), which has its own skill, and it does not decide which browser to use.
- anthropic-skills:computer-use: Read this skill before the first step of any request to do something in an app on the person's own computer (Notes, Finder, System Settings, any desktop app), to look at their screen, or for "computer use". Computer use (desktop control) lets Claude take screenshots of the person's desktop and control it with clicks, typing and scrolling through the Claude desktop app; its tools are named mcp__computer-use__* when the session runs in the desktop app and mcp__remote-devices__computer_* when a cloud session is linked to the person's computer; before computer use is turned on for a conversation there may be no such tools, only an enable__mcp__remote-devices__computer tool, which turns it on. It covers turning it on, picking the right tool, the access flow, and the safety rules for tiered apps, links and financial actions. It is not for websites, which go through Claude in Chrome or the built-in browser and their own skills.
- anthropic-skills:consolidate-memory: Reflective pass over your memory files — merge duplicates, fix stale facts, prune the index.
- anthropic-skills:deep-research: Use this skill when the user's prompt requires (1) researching a topic across multiple sources, comparing options or alternatives, analyzing trends or history, understanding markets or industries, or reviewing literature or studies and (2) synthesizing that research into a comprehensive, narrative report. If you're planning to search the web or internal knowledge bases, consider using this skill. This skill coordinates research subagents, so use it only when you have a tool for spawning subagents (the Agent or Task tool); otherwise, research the question directly.
- anthropic-skills:docs: docs (editable docs people share and comment on; the default for any document, named as a doc or not: a document, report, proposal, resume, cover letter, letter, contract, policy, form, template, worksheet, essay, handbook, guide, how-to, cheat sheet, SOP or other writing to keep, share, collaborate on, send, submit, print or sign; a doc exports to Word, PDF, Markdown or Google Docs, so needing a file to send, attach, upload, submit or print is no reason to pick Word, and a file nobody asked for is a doc, not Word; a plan, comparison, summary or notes asked in chat stays in chat; a pasted claude.ai artifact link may be a doc: check with docs tools first; Word or another file format named, tracked changes wanted, or a .docx to change or use as a template → that format's skill): making one → if no docs-connector instructions are in context, call its `guide` (topic.instructions) first; then create the doc (headings only, no body) before any search, file read or plan, even with files attached.
- anthropic-skills:docx: Use this skill whenever the user wants to create, read, edit, or manipulate Word documents (.docx) or Word templates (.dotx). Triggers include: any mention of Microsoft Word Documents, such as 'Word doc', 'word document', '.docx', '.dotx', 'microsoft doc'. Also use when extracting or reorganizing content from .docx or .dotx files, inserting or replacing images in documents, find-and-replace in Word files, working with tracked changes or comments, or converting content into a polished Word document. If the user asks for a deliverable as a Word or .docx file (to download, email or print), use this skill. However, if they ask for a document, page, report, memo, or notes WITHOUT naming a file format and the session offers Claude's own dedicated document or page skill or connector, use that instead, even if they will email or print it. Do NOT use for PDFs, spreadsheets, Google Docs, or coding unrelated to document generation.
- anthropic-skills:explain-usage: Explain where this session's tokens went, with one simple chart in plain language. Use when the user says things like "explain my usage", "where did my tokens go", or asks for a usage breakdown.
- anthropic-skills:google-workspace: Read this before the first Google Drive, Docs, Sheets or Slides connector call whenever the task creates or changes a Google file. Use this skill whenever the user wants to create or change a Google Doc, Sheet or Slides file in their Google Drive. Triggers include: a request that names Google Docs, Sheets, Slides or Drive and asks to make, edit, format, copy or rename a file; a docs.google.com link with a request to change that file, even a one-line fix or suggested edits; and any follow-up change to a Google file from earlier in the chat, even "change it" or "add a tab". Includes helper scripts for document positions, cell ranges and slide layout. However, if the user asks for a doc, deck or spreadsheet without naming Google, or gives a Google file only as source material for something new, use Claude's own output type instead. Do NOT use for read-only questions about a Google file, or for Word, Excel, PowerPoint or PDF files.
- anthropic-skills:import-memory: Import a memory export from another AI assistant into Claude's memory — conversationally, additively, and with the content treated as data.
- anthropic-skills:morning: Render the user's morning brief as a styled HTML artifact, or set it up as a recurring weekday task. This includes reading or extracting text/tables from PDFs, combining or merging multiple PDFs into one, splitting PDFs apart, rotating pages, adding watermarks, creating new PDFs, filling PDF forms, encrypting/decrypting PDFs, extracting images, and OCR on scanned PDFs to make them searchable. If the user mentions a .pdf file or asks to produce one, use this skill.
- anthropic-skills:pptx: Use this skill any time a .pptx or .potx file is involved in any way — as input, output, or both. This includes: creating slide decks, pitch decks, or presentations as PowerPoint (.pptx) files; reading, parsing, or extracting text from any .pptx or .potx file (even if the extracted content will be used elsewhere, like in an email, summary, or creating a different type of slide deck); editing, modifying, or updating existing presentations; combining or splitting slide files; working with templates (.potx), layouts, speaker notes, or comments. Trigger whenever the user asks for a PowerPoint or .pptx file, or references a .pptx or .potx filename, regardless of what they plan to do with the content afterward. However, when the user asks for a deck, slides, a slide deck, or a presentation without naming a file format, default to using a dedicated slide-deck artifact type or a separate slides skill if this session offers one; otherwise, use this skill.

- anthropic-skills:skill-creator: Create new skills, modify and improve existing skills, and measure skill performance. - anthropic-skills:xlsx: Use this skill any time a spreadsheet file is the primary input or output. This means any task where the user wants to: open, read, edit, or fix an existing .xlsx, .xlsm, .xltx, .csv, or .tsv file (e.g., adding columns, computing formulas, formatting, charting, cleaning messy data); create a new spreadsheet from scratch or from other data sources; or convert between tabular file formats. Trigger especially when the user references a spreadsheet file by name or path — even casually (like "the xlsx in my downloads") — and wants something done to it or produced from it. Also trigger for cleaning or restructuring messy tabular data files (malformed rows, misplaced headers, junk data) into proper spreadsheets. The deliverable must be a spreadsheet file. Do NOT trigger when the primary deliverable is a Word document, HTML report, standalone Python script, database pipeline, or Google Sheets API integration, even if tabular data is involved.
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. When the destination is a first-party document connector (host-designated, never self-described) that renders live charts, hand it the rows (inline, or as an uploaded data file the chart cites) rather than a rendered PNG/SVG — a picture of a chart loses hover, data inspection and per-value comments. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's.
